articleTitle: Evaluating an alternate layout for the SKA-Low aperture array stations using Computational Electromagnetic simulations
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The current prototype station for the SKA-Low radio telescope consists of a large number of antennas quasi-randomly distributed in close proximity to one another. An alternate, more uniform distribution of antennas is introduced, and preliminary simulation results are shown. This layout is under consideration as a possible replacement of the quasi-random positioning of the antennas. The main motivation for this new layout is to avoid pairs of antennas almost touching each other, which has a negative impact on the antenna pattern. The individual and station patterns are presented for the two layouts and show that the higher regularity in antenna distribution has beneficial effects, although there are other considerations which must be taken into account.

articleTitle: Preconditioners for Multi-Screen Scattering
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In this contribution, a well-conditioned method for the modelling of scattering by so-called multi-screens or PEC sheets including junctions is introduced. The method starts from the inflated screen approach by Claeys and Hiptmair. We introduce a Calderón preconditioner and a suitable discretisation scheme. The resulting scheme contains many more DoFs than strictly required. We will show how almost all redundancy can be removed without significant loss of effectiveness of the method.

articleTitle: Hierarchical Vector Bases for Pyramid Cells
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: This presentation summarizes a very simple and straightforward new procedure to build hierarchical vector-bases for the pyramid that conform to those used on adjacent differently shaped cells (tetrahedra, hexahedron and triangular prisms). Our new curl- and divergence-conforming bases, together with the corresponding curls and divergences, have simple and easy to implement mathematical expressions. Results confirming faster convergence and avoidance of spurious modes/solutions will be reported at the conference.

articleTitle: High Isolation 4-Port UWB MIMO Antenna with Novel Decoupling Structure for High Speed and 5G Communication
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In this manuscript, CPW fed 4-port multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) antenna is designed to cover the ultra-wideband (UWB) range and beyond. The proposed structure has a compact volumetric size of 50x50x1.6 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. The novel decoupling structure is used to improve the isolation <-20dB across the entire operating band ranging from 3.34 to 14.67 GHz. The realized average gain of the antenna is 3.37 dBi and the corresponding radiation efficiency is more than 70 % throughout the usable frequency band. The radiation patterns at 4.51, 6.91, 8.25 and 10.12 GHz are evaluated and found acceptable for the UWB applications. The diversity parameters envelope correlation coefficient (ECC) and diversity gain (DG) are calculated and found $\lt 0.005$ and $\gt 9.97$ dB, respectively across the operating band. The MIMO design is optimized and results are calculated using CST Microwave studio. The proposed MIMO antenna is suitable for UWB wireless systems, 5G (lower band), and other high-speed communication devices.

articleTitle: Iterative DGFM Solver Extensions for Fast Sparse Array Analysis
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: This paper considers the efficient method of moments (MoM) solution of large irregular sparse antenna arrays consisting of disjoint identical perfect electric conducting antennas, via an iterative solution scheme utilising only localised solutions. The scheme is based on the domain Green’s function method (DGFM). Two algorithmic extensions are proposed. The first is tiling, which reduces the required number of local solutions and thus also the computational cost. The second is an error-approximation step, which accelerates iterative convergence.

articleTitle: Digital Beamforming System for SKA Low Frequency Aperture array
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Digital beamforming system based on Chinese Tile Processing Module version 2 (CTPM-v2) developed by KLAASA is a digital beamforming back-end processor for SKA low frequency aperture array. Digital beamforming system supports multiple beamforming in quanta of up to 128 channels of analog signal with maximum 300MHz instantaneous bandwidth. A series of experiment results show that the system has a very good long-time stability, and the channelization characteristics meet the design requirements. KLAASA realized simultaneous 8 beams forming by this system. As the software and firmware of digital beamforming system can be customized according to different requirements, digital beamforming system is suitable for different types of low-frequency aperture array, which is conducive to promoting the development of digital array radio telescopes.

articleTitle: Bilateral quadrature wireless coil for breast MRI
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In this paper, we demonstrate a quadrature radiofrequency wireless coil to improve breast MRI at 1.5 T. The coil is based on the combination of the metamaterial-inspired resonator and Helmholtz-type resonator. Numerical and experimental studies of the bilateral quadrature coil have shown that it increases the transmit efficiency of the whole-body birdcage coil by 7-fold and radiofrequency safety by 4.3 times.

articleTitle: Waveguide Filter Miniaturization with Metallic Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In this paper, the miniaturization performance of waveguide bandpass filters loaded with three different periodic metallic metasurfaces is studied. The effective refractive index of holey structure, pin-loaded holes, and glide-symmetric metallic pins and their effects on the compactness of K/Ka band filters are investigated. In the glide-symmetric filter, a fourth-degree Chebyshev response with the center frequency of 28 GHz, bandwidth of 3 GHz, return loss of 20 dB, insertion loss of 0.4 dB, and the size reduction of 41.3% is achieved.

articleTitle: Design of 94GHz series-fed microstrip antenna array
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: A 8×8 microstrip antenna array for W-band application is presented in this paper. The Taylor distribution is employed as the excitation amplitude coefficients of each patch, which can allow the antenna array to achieve lower sidelobe level (SLL). A 1 to 8 substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) power divider is proposed to feed the 8×8 radiation patches. The radiation elements and the SIW feed network are on the same layer. The antenna array shows good performance at W-band with the center frequency 94GHz. At 94GHz, S11 of the power divider is less than -20dB and S21~S91 are greater than -10.5dB. The simulation results show that the antenna array has a peak gain of 22dB at 94GHz.

articleTitle: An Analytical-Numerical MAR Technique for the Analysis of the Plane Wave Scattering from a Circular Hole in a Thin Resistive Plate
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In this paper, the analysis of the plane wave scattering from a circular hole in a thin resistive plate is formulated in terms of a suitable set of dual singular integral equations in the vector Hankel transform domain discretized by using the Helmholtz-Galerkin technique in order to obtain fast-converging and highly computationally efficient matrix equations of the Fredholm second kind.

articleTitle: Preliminary investigation into the use of silver seed layers in copper electroplating of waveguide parts
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: We present a preliminary investigation into the copper plating of printed SLA plastics using a silver seed layer. The silver seed layer is deposited using the Tollens reaction, a chemical process used to test for aldehydes. The device under test is a split-block WR42 waveguide cut along the E-plane, manufactured with SLA printing. Initial results showed that the waveguide achieved a loss of better than 5.6 dB/m over the operating band. Repeatability was an issue with multiple waveguides exhibiting corrosion and high insertion loss.

articleTitle: Design of W-band substrate integrated waveguide slit antenna array
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In this paper, a high-efficiency W-band $8 \times 8$ substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) slit antenna array is designed. The antenna radiation feed structure is ideal electric conductor layer, coupling waveguide, coupling layer, radiating waveguide, and radiation layer from bottom to top, respectively. The radiation layer antenna is an $8 \times 8$ slit antenna array, which is formed by the arrangement and combination of 8 rows of single waveguides, each single waveguide corresponds to a feed port, and the energy enters the coupling waveguide from the feed source, and couples the energy into the radiation waveguide through the tilted slit of the coupling layer. The slit antenna array is simulated and optimized by 3D simulation software, the dielectric substrate is uniformly Rogers 5880, and the maximum gain of the SIW slit antenna array is 21.07 dB when the operating frequency is 94 GHz, and the -10 dB bandwidth of the antenna is $93.96 \sim 96.11$ GHz with a bandwidth of 2.15 GHz.

articleTitle: Bandwidth Enhancement of a Substrate Integrated Waveguide Dielectric Resonator Antenna using Metallic Shorting Vias
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: A D-band Substrate Integrated Waveguide (SIW) fed Dielectric Resonator Antenna (DRA) is proposed. The dielectric resonator (DR) is designed to operate in higher order modes. Impedance matching techniques are used to merge these resonance modes to increase the bandwidth of the antenna. Simulation results show that the antenna exhibits a-10 dB impedance bandwidth between 138.27GHz and 150.95GHz, equivalent to 9%. The proposed antenna has a maximum gain of 8.79dBi and a radiation efficiency of 81%.

articleTitle: Multi-Band Light-Matter Interaction in hBN-Based Metasurface Absorber
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: This paper presents a multi-band metamaterial-based absorber using phononic two-dimensional (2D) material. The structure consists of a top hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) layer on an aluminum nanograting structure deposited on a dielectric slab waveguide and a thick metallic reflector forming an MIM (metal-insulator-metal) configuration. The proposed absorber exhibits a hyperbolic phonon polariton (HPPs) in hBN, surface plasmon (SP) modes in the spacer (ZnTe: zinc telluride), and Fabry-Perot resonances in the MIM configuration, resulting in five sharp, high absorption peaks in the mid-infrared (MIR) spectral range. The proposed multi-band absorber can be utilized in various applications, ranging from optical detection devices to multispectral thermoelectric volt.

articleTitle: Radiofrequency wave absorption in a graded-index GNP-treated cancer cell substrate inserted in a waveguide
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The heating of biological tissue with inserted gold nanoparticles (GNPs) by radiofrequency (RF) electromagnetic radiation is an important phenomenon with potential to be used as a non-invasive method to treat cancer. The method relies on the cancer cells’ property to intake an abnormal amount of nutrients. If GNPs are coated with suitable nutrient ligands, they can be taken into the cancer cells with high concentration, while their concentration in normal cells remains low. Consequently, the temperature of cells with high GNP concentration will increase to such levels to cause the death of such (cancer) cells under exposure of an externally applied RF field as the GNPs are driven into electrophoretic motion.

articleTitle: A Study on the Polarization Dependence of Backward Transient Scattering by a Two-Dimensional Coated Conducting Cylinder Using the TD-SPT
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The study on high-frequency (HF) electromagnetic wave scattering by a two-dimensional (2-D) conducting cylinder covered with a dielectric medium layer (2-D coated conducting cylinder) has become an important research topic [1]–[3].

articleTitle: Influence of Antenna Systems with Metamaterial Screens Composition and Geometric Parameters on Mutual Coupling Between Antennas
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In practice antenna systems comprising a large number of antennas of different ranges and purposes. Moreover, from the point of view of providing electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) each antennas location object is a unique object distinguished in both composition of antennas and their arrangement [1, 2]. Accordingly, the task of reduction of mutual coupling between antennas is very difficult and needs to be solved in each case over again.

articleTitle: Extended Near-Field Capabilities for the Compact Antenna Test Range at the University of Pretoria
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The rapid evolution of wireless connectivity has brought about new measurement challenges in the field of antenna testing. On a previous occasion, it has been reported how a mobile cylindrical near-field scanner has been introduced into the anechoic chamber that houses the compact antenna test range at the University of Pretoria [1]. This system has been used very successfully over a number of years now for the evaluation of cellular base-station antennas that would otherwise have been too large for the compact range. The measurement system has continuously been extended, with spherical near-field scanning being one of the substantial recent additions. This mode of operation is very useful for the measurement of smaller indoor base-station antennas as well as for the characterization of near-field probes and standard-gain antennas.

articleTitle: On the Fast Direct Solution of a Preconditioned Electromagnetic Integral Equation
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: This work presents a fast direct solver strategy for electromagnetic integral equations in the high-frequency regime. The new scheme relies on a suitably preconditioned combined field formulation and results in a single skeleton form plus identity equation. This is obtained after a regularization of the elliptic spectrum through the extraction of a suitably chosen equivalent circulant problem. The inverse of the system matrix is then obtained by leveraging the Woodbury matrix identity, the low-rank representation of the extracted part of the operator, and fast circulant algebra yielding a scheme with a favorable complexity and suitable for the solution of multiple right-hand sides. Theoretical considerations are accompanied by numerical results both of which are confirming and showing the practical relevance of the newly developed scheme.

articleTitle: Synthesis of an inhomogeneous anisotropic impedance plane from several reflected waves
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In this work, a two-dimensional problem of synthesizing an inhomogeneous anisotropic impedance plane that reflects a wave incident at a given angle in the required number of directions on a circular polarization is solved for the first time. The anisotropic structure is realized by a frequent array of orthogonal impedance strips adjacent to each other, oriented at an angle on the plane. Formulas for reflection coefficients are given. The problem of synthesis is solved on the basis of the reciprocity principle. The laws of distribution of reactances and their orientation are obtained in the approximation of physical optics in an explicit form. The problem of analysis for verification of the obtained formulas is solved strictly by the method of integral equations. The results of numerical calculations are presented.

articleTitle: An Automatic Mesh Refinement Method Based on Phase Extracted Basis Functions for Electromagnetic Scattering Analysis of Electrically Extra-Large Objects
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Electromagnetic (EM) scattering problems are commonly solved by numerical methods such as the finite element method (FEM) and the method of moments (MoM). In a numerical simulation, the solution domain needs to be discretized into small mesh elements. The quality of the mesh is critical for the solution accuracy. While a denser mesh with smaller elements can result in a better numerical accuracy, it also leads to higher computational and storage costs, making it expensive to solve scattering problems from electrically large objects. To reduce such costs, higher order basis functions (HOBFs) [1] have been developed and applied in EM analysis. By expanding the amplitude of the induced surface currents with the HOBFs, larger mesh elements can be used, which reduce effectively the total number of unknowns required in solving an EM problem. For objects with smooth and convex surfaces, it has been shown in [2] that describing the phase variation of the induced surface currents can reduce the total number of unknowns even more effectively. By incorporating a traveling wave phase factor into the traditionally used low-order curvilinear Rao-Wilton-Glisson (RWG) basis functions, the resulting phase extracted basis functions (PEBFs) can be defined on mesh elements as large as half a wavelength. The combination of the PEBFs and HOBFs can reduce the number of unknowns by two orders of magnitude, which improved the simulation efficiency significantly while maintaining a good numerical accuracy [3].

articleTitle: Progress towards a planar integrated 22 GHz radiometer for water vapour radiometry
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Atmospheric water vapour can delay and attenuate the reception of astronomical sources and impede radio astronomy observations [1]. Water vapour radiometers have found use in both phase correction due to water vapour induced delay and in site surveying for potential radio astronomy sites.

articleTitle: A non-conformal multi-resolution preconditioner in the MoM solution of large multi-scale structures
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The extension of the surface integral equations (SIEs) [1] to non-conforming meshes has ignited intense research in the last years with the goal of finding a versatile and accurate method to address large and multi-scale complex problems, greatly simplifying computer-aided-design (CAD) generation and meshing processes.

articleTitle: Phaseless Bi-spherical Near-field Measurement
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: To overcome the challenge of acquiring high-precision phase information in spherical near-field measurements, this paper treats the solution of the spherical mode coefficients (SMC) as a phase recovery problem. Targeting the two critical factors that determine the converting accuracy, that is, the phase recovery algorithm and the near-field sampling strategy, by comparing the error of the extrapolated far field, this paper identifies a phase recovery algorithm most appropriate for phaseless near-field measurement, and an adapted spherical sampling approach. The numerical results demonstrate that Reweighted Amplitude Flow integrated with the bi-spherical sampling strategy is capable of sufficiently retrieving the SMC and deriving the high-precision radiation characteristics of the antenna under test (AUT).

articleTitle: Efficiency of a 3D Metallic Antenna on top of Finite Ground Plane and Soil
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The evaluation of noise coming from the soil to the antenna is of paramount concern in radioastronomy. The noise power can be derived from the antenna efficiency calculated as the ratio of the power radiated in the air to the total power fed at the antenna ports. In this paper, we compute the efficiency of the SKALA2 antenna while accounting for the finite ground plane and the lossy soil. A Method of Moments simulation tool based on inhomogeneous plane waves is used to account for the interactions between the antenna and the ground plane in the vicinity of a semi-infinite homogeneous soil. This tool is used to obtain the antenna efficiency and directivity at zenith across frequency considering different soil permittivities and finite ground plane sizes.

articleTitle: Railway Environmental Scenario Recognition for GNSS Localization based on Deep Learning and Vit Model
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The environmental scenario along the railway can be categorized as tunnel, open area, urban canyon etc. As the train moves, the environment is changing and challenging which may influence Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) accuracy. Environment scenarios have different characteristics, which are the main ground error source for GNSS. In order to improve GNSS for train localization robustness, it is necessary to recognize environment characteristics in each environment scenario. The GNSS receiver delivers position result information obeying NMEA-0183 protocol, PRN, azimuth, elevation and SNR (Signal-to-noise-ratio) etc. Such information can be regarded as parameters to describe the environment scenario. Thus, it is meaningful to generate the heatmap state of the scenario by collecting satellite observations, using interpolation and position transformation. We train the heatmap dataset based on the Vision Transformer (ViT) model to recognize the actual receiver scenario. The overall accuracy of the model in the validation set is 88.7%.

articleTitle: Over-the-Air System Noise Temperature Measurement of Active Integrated Antennas in a Reverberation Chamber
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Low noise receivers play an essential role in wireless systems in radio astronomy and 5G/6G applications. Especially in radioastronomy, the received signal strength is very weak. Therefore, maintaining a good Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) is quite important. A known concept to reduce the system noise temperature is to use noise matching for the Low-Noise Amplifier (LNA) and the antenna to get the optimal SNR. Due to the integrated nature of these systems, it is challenging to measure the noise performance of the total system accurately. For example, existing methods such as the Radiometric or the G/T method can be sensitive to inaccuracies due to the dependency on the sky noise temperature, the radiation pattern of the antenna, or the size of the antenna [1, 2]. Therefore we developed a new method, which can estimate the Noise Figure (NF) of a wireless system over-the-air (OTA), independent of these factors. The new method uses the Reverberation Chamber (RC) to create a consistent and repeatable environment. The uniform behavior of the RC makes the method independent of the radiation pattern of the antenna. This method measures the integrated antenna as one system, so the efficiency of the antenna, the NF of the LNA, and the noise matching between the Antenna and LNA are all taken into account.

articleTitle: Detailed Design of an 18-45 GHz Multi-Purpose Radio Astronomy Receiver
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: We report on recent developments in the design of a sideband separating radio astronomy receiver operating from 18 - 45 GHz, implemented as a multi-chip module (MCM) on RF laminate, with analogue sideband calibration. The sideband rejection calibration achieves a simulated, mean sideband rejection improvement of 5 dB in comparison with a receiver without calibration, evaluated over a 1 GHz frequency resolution. The minimum simulated rejection is 15 dB at the IF band edges, with an average of 25 dB rejection mid-band. A back-end converter design for testing the receiver is also presented.

articleTitle: Detection of HRP at microwave frequency with functionalized graphene film
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: A microstrip antenna based sensor for the detection of the concentration of Horseradish peroxidase (HRP) is presented. The sensor is composed of a microstrip antenna connected to a stub with a gap and a graphene film deposited in the gap. The graphene film is deposited by doctor blading it into a designated position. The surface of the film is functionalized for HRP. In this paper, high concentrations of HRP are detected by the variation of the reflection coefficient of the antenna.

articleTitle: Curved 3-D Frequency-Selective Rasorber
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Frequency selective rasorber is a concept combining absorber and radome, which is often used to absorb undesired out-of-band electromagnetic (EM) waves, while maintaining transparency in the required frequencies. Many rasorbers have been designed in a planar structure for easily fabrication. However, a curved rasorber is often desired for many practical applications. Moreover, it is important to design a rasorber that can be integrated with antenna systems.

articleTitle: Frequency Ripple in Antenna Noise Temperature of Small Offset Gregorian Reflector Systems
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Radiation pattern based responses such as the antenna noise temperature, aperture efficiency and the receiving sensitivity of electrically small offset Gregorian dual reflector antenna systems exhibit, as part of their underlying functional form, a chromatic aberration (ripple) over the operating frequency band. During design iterations, this ripple is often ignored as a prohibitively large set of frequency samples is required to accurately characterise it. Additionally, the ripple has a comparatively low amplitude relative to the overall response, which suggests that accounting for its effects may have a small impact on the general accuracy of a calculated metric. However, highly optimised radio telescopes may require an accurate characterisation of a reflector system for their design. Therefore, this paper investigates the ripple component and the effect it has on the computation of the receiving sensitivity.

articleTitle: An Error Analysis of the Three-Term Recurrence Relation of the Modal Green Function
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The scattering by perfectly electric conducting (PEC) axis-symmetric objects, so-called bodies of revolution (BORs), is a famous problem in electromagnetics. One approach to characterize the electromagnetic scattering of such kind of structures is based on the electric field integral equation (EFIE), whose core is a specific integral operator known as the Modal Green function (MGF). The MGF of the EFIE exhibits a singular behavior when having the source and observation points close to each other.

articleTitle: Simulated Performance of Antenna Position Estimation through Sub-Sampled Exponential Analysis
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Antenna position estimation is an important problem in large irregular arrays where the positions might not be known very accurately from the start. In a previous paper we presented a method using harmonically related signals transmitted from an Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV), with the added advantage that the UAV can be in the near-field of the receiving antenna array. It was shown that the method delivers excellent results using ideal synthetic data with added noise. In this paper we continue the work by simulating the problem in a full-wave solver. Although the results are less accurate than when synthetic data are used, due to the effects of mutual coupling, the method still performs satisfactorily, with errors smaller than 4% of the smallest transmitted wavelength.

articleTitle: A Novel Time-Domain Asymptotic Solution for a Backward Transient Scattered Electric Field by a Coated Metal Cylinder
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel high frequency method for a backward transient scattered electric field by a metal cylinder covered with a lossless dielectric medium layer (coated metal cylinder). A time-domain (TD) asymptotic solution, which is referred to as a TD Fourier transform method (TD-FTM), is derived by applying the FTM to a backward transient scattered electric field expressed by an integral form. The TD-FTM is represented by a combination of a direct geometric optical ray (DGO) and a reflected GO (RGO) series, where each field component is given by a closed form. The accuracy and practicality of the TD-FTM are evaluated by comparing it with three reference solutions.

articleTitle: Application of a Magneto-Dielectric Absorber to the Antenna Feed Cable
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The presence of the antenna feed cable is very often a significant source of changes in antenna parameters in relation to the ideal antenna. In the antenna radiation field, there appears an element whose size most often exceeds the largest linear size of the antenna. In the case of a straight dipole, only the presence of a cable routed in a plane perpendicular to the dipole, passing through the center of the dipole, does not change the parameters of the dipole antenna. In any other case, such changes will occur. If the feed cable is too close to the antenna components, the presence of this cable may prevent normal use of the antenna. Running the feed cable in a plane perpendicular to the antenna is cumbersome and usually subject to significant limitations, leading to the necessity to take into account and accept undesirable changes in antenna parameters.

articleTitle: Conversion from LP to CP by a tunable FSS with Embedded Microstrip Lines as Feeding Network
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The design of a tunable Frequency Selective Surface (FSS) structure by means of PIN diodes is presented in this paper. Some significant FSS-related applications such as polarization control, polarization filtering, and spatial filtering are represented in the frequency band from 2 to 14 GHz. Using of a control network (CN) as a new configuration for biasing the active elements to compensate the symmetry breaking is also suggested.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Active Implantable Medical Device RF-Induced Heating in the Vicinity of an Orthopedic Plate during MRI
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: This paper evaluates the magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) radiofrequency (RF)-induced heating, in terms of Ig-averaged specific absorption rate (SAR), of an active implantable medical device (AIMD) when it is placed near an orthopedic plate device at 10 different configurations. The SAR values of the AIMD are evaluated with the transfer function approach and direct numerical simulations. It shows that the results obtained by the transfer function method are in good agreement with those obtained by direct simulations. This indicates that the transfer function method is still a valid approach for RF-induced heating evaluation in the presence of nearby metallic devices.

articleTitle: Modeling the instrumental contribution of a radio telescope to astronomical polarization measurements: the Mueller matrix approach
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The challenge in radioastronomical polarimetry is the accurate measurement of a weak polarized signal embedded in a (usually) much stronger unpolarized signal. The imperfection of the telescope, such as its cross-polarization, sidelobes, beam squint, and beam squash, alters the polarization state of the incoming radiation and converts unpolarized signal to apparently polarized signal [1]. From an astronomer’s perspective, the radio telescope causes the Stokes parameters of the incoming signal to leak into one another. Such leakage can jeopardize the reliability of an observation [2, 3].

articleTitle: A review of state-of-the-art radio technology for 21-cm cosmology experiments
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: 21-cm cosmology is promising a plethora of discoveries about the early Universe in the coming years. The SKA telescope will, in a few years, have unprecedented imaging capabilities and will aim at producing detailed tomographic studies of the Cosmic Dawn and the subsequent Epoch-of-Reionization via observations of the redshifted 21-cm line from atomic Hydrogen. Before the SKA comes online, and since a few years ago, smaller single-antenna and interferometric radio experiments are already paving the way and hinting at a potential detection of the 21-cm line, both in its sky-averaged and power spectra components.

articleTitle: A Wavelength-Selective Multilayer Absorber for Heat Signature Control
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Engineering the thermal radiation using wavelength-selective thermal emitters is of great importance in the field of thermophotovoltaics, radiative cooling, and heat signature control. In this paper, a wavelength-selective Vanadium/Germanium (V/Ge) multilayer absorber is demonstrated. The proposed design realizes a perfect absorption at the resonance wavelength of 5870 nm, placed within the nonatmospheric window (5-8 μ m) while maintaining low absorptivity within the atmospheric windows. It is verified that the proposed emitter represents angle insensitive feature for oblique incidence up to 60° for both transverse magnetic (TM) and transverse electric (TE) polarizations.

articleTitle: Considering Model Excitations for the Density-Taper Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The density-taper algorithm as proposed almost 60 years ago, and until the mid-1990s was arguably the best algorithm for synthesising thinned antenna arrays. However, the effect of the model excitation on the performance of the density-taper algorithm has not received much attention. The use of a number of window functions as model excitations was evaluated, and it was found that the filling factor of the model excitation has a significant effect on the results obtained. Two approaches to modifying model excitations to achieve desirable filling factors are presented and compared. The Taylor window function is shown to produce excellent results, especially when appropriately modified using the proposed techniques.

articleTitle: Smart Hat Antenna For Wifi Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: A new antenna structure called Smart Hat Antenna (SHA) with about 16.67 % bandwidth is presented. The antenna is composed of a central common reflector surrounded by multiple monopoles, both positioned on a ground plane. By keeping the beamwidth and resonant frequency constant, one monopole element is connected at a time to achieve beam switching. Then, eight beams are generated, covering the entire azimuth plane with a peak gain of 7.5 dB for θmax=90° (i.e. elevation of 0°). Only 1.72 dB is lost in overlap.

articleTitle: Antenna Placement Analysis on SA Navy MMIPV
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: This paper presents an antenna placement analysis and optimization approach which was conducted for two new South African Navy (SAN) vessel types. The design and construction of these vessels fall under SAN Projects HOTEL and BIRO. Naval vessels typically have requirements for many antennas (e.g. communications, navigation, radar) to be placed in close proximity to one another, due to the limited space available for their placement. Antenna placement optimization is therefore a vital step in the design of a naval vessel in order to ensure the correct installed performance, and as well as acceptable levels of mutual interference (i.e. co-located performance) is achieved.

articleTitle: Research on the Effect of Traction Return Current on Locomotive Signal Equipment
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The structure of traction network consists of contact wire, messenger wire, positive feeder, protection wire, ground wire and rail. The positive feeder and protection wire usually descend from high altitude to low altitude above the ground in the station due to space constraint. In this case, the traction return current in the positive feeder and protection wire will change and may cause interference to signal equipment. In this paper, the maximum disturbance voltage received by the locomotive signal antenna is obtained. The simulation results of the coupling disturbance voltage are compared with the field measurement data, and the envelope is consistent. The minimum protection distance from positive feeder and protection wire to track center is given to maintain the normal operation of locomotive signal equipment.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Modeling of Nonlinear Graphene-Based Nanostructures
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: We present here several advanced numerical methods, including both time-domain numerical methods and frequency-domain numerical methods, to numerically study the electromagnetic (EM) response of nonlinear graphene-based structures. In the case of time-domain method, we incorporate a nonlinear generalized source into the finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method to study a wide frequency-range response of nonlinear graphene-based nanostructures. In the case of frequency-domain method, we would detail the approaches to solve the frequency-domain nonlinear coupling equations for EM modeling of nonlinear graphene-based nanostructure by using the finite element method (FEM) and coupled-mode theory (CMT). To verify the accuracy of the developed numerical methods, two numerical examples are given in the end.

articleTitle: TE-type Natural Complex Oscillations in 2D Arbitrarily Shaped Slotted Cavities
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Studies of the natural complex oscillations in 2D slotted cavities of arbitrary shapes are pivotal in the prediction of the resonance response from variously shaped jet engine intakes. The complex eigenvalues of these oscillations can also be regarded as cut-off relative wave numbers bf the short-circuited waveguides. This circumstance makes studies on this subject even more relevant. These studies are based on the non-trivial rigorous solution of the scattering problem for perfectly electrically conducting (PEC) slotted cavities of arbitrary shape, excited by an obliquely incident H-polarized plane wave (see Fig.1).

articleTitle: Design approaches for compact airborne COMINT DF antenna arrays
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The prospect of deploying Communications Intelligence (COMINT) direction finding (DF) payloads on small manned and autonomous aircraft as well as aerostats has seen increasing interest in recent years. To this end, there is a temptation in the industry to repurpose existing compact COMINT DF systems designed for land/sea mobile and even manpack use to airborne missions. Even in the case of purpose-designed systems, though specific consideration might be given to uniquely airborne requirements such as aerodynamics, low profile and compact size, the array design approach itself might typically follow that of a land-based counterpart and can fail to account for specific differences in the signal environment and capability expectations of the airborne electromagnetic mission.

articleTitle: Machine-Learning for Optimization of Electrodes and Waveforms for Electroporation
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The adoption of high-frequency irreversible electroporation in a variety of medical treatments is more and more frequent. Unfortunately, a large number of parameters can influence the efficiency and effectiveness of the electroporation procedures: suitable choices of electrodes and of the stimulating signals being some important examples.In this paper, we demonstrate that machine-learning strategies based on Neural Networks are an appropriate approach to optimize the choice of the electrode characteristics, and we discuss the extension of alternative Machine Learning approaches to the optimization of the stimulating waveforms.

articleTitle: Freely tailoring far-field spin-polarized wavefronts with surface wave metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Surface waves (SWs) are eigen electromagnetic (EM) modes bounded at the surface of optical materials/devices, e.g., metals, semiconductors and dielectric waveguides. Distinct from another fundamental EM mode, i.e., propagating waves (PWs) in free-space, SWs possess the intriguing optical characteristics of subwavelength resolution and local-field enhancement, offering us numerous applications such as sub-diffraction imaging, optical sensor, plasmonic laser, on-chip plasmonic circuit, enhanced nonlinear optics. For the on-chip photonic applications, the far-field emissions of localized SWs in some plasmonic devices usually rely on Bragg devices, which however suffer from several fundamental limitations, including wavelength-scale manipulations, multiple mode generation, lack of control abilities for radiation amplitude, phase and polarization.

articleTitle: A new perturbation approach to quantifying changes in the far field pattern induced by rounding the corners of a scatterer
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The electromagnetic fields diffracted by sharp edges and comers have long been understood to be different in character to those scattered by smooth bodies. The nature of the singularities in the field and its derivatives is described in [1], Although analytical and numerical methods for the accurate modelling of these singularities have had substantial development, their implementation can be both time consuming and rather specialised. On the other hand, the large number of readily available general purpose scattering packages generally assume that the scattering surface is smooth, and in order to model scattering from an obstacle with comers it is usually replaced by a smooth scatterer resulting from rounding the comers in some fashion. Although the singularities in the field quantities and surface distributions are thereby eliminated, it is desirable to develop some estimate of the error or difference thus induced.

articleTitle: Enhanced Terahertz Smith-Purcell Radiation with a Novel Grating
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: When a high-speed electron beam passes close to the surface of a mental grating, due to Smith-Purcell effect an electromagnetic radiation from the grating can be observed [1]. The Smith-Purcell radiation (SPR) arises from oscillating dipoles composed of the passing electrons and their image charges in the grating [2]. In general, if the grating period is designed in millimeter (mm) or sub-mm scale, the SPR generated will be in terahertz (THz) band. However, SPR is a type of incoherent radiation with weak radiation energy, which limits its application in developing THz sources. Herein, we propose a novel grating in Figure 1 to improve the coherence of THz SRP. Unlike the common rectangular grating where the electron beam can only move above it and induce image electrons along the plane, the novel annular grating enables the electron beam to move through its center and hence induce circularly distributed image electrons surrounding the beam. This special design can also enhance the interaction between the electron beam and the electromagnetic surface wave. Furthermore, we have conducted numerical simulations with the CST to compare the radiation energy distributions between the rectangular grating and the novel one. Apparently, in the rectangular grating case, all the fundamental, second and third harmonics in the THz band are observable over a wide range of observation angle, indicating an incoherent SRP. As to the novel grating case, the third harmonic is hardly recognized due to its lower energy, while both the fundamental and second harmonics are well bunched in a fairly small angle with higher energies, implying a coherent THz radiation. As a consequence, the novel annular grating is promising to enhance the THz SPR.

articleTitle: Contemporary EMC Investigations on some South African Science Projects
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: This industry paper describes two contemporary investigations with strong electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) requirements in South Africa:•new installation magnetic noise evaluation at the South African National Space Agency (SANSA) Space Science Centre (former Hermanus Magnetic Observatory) and,•stringent shielding effectiveness (SE) testing of the MeerKAT Telescope Array, which will form part of the international Square Kilometre Array (SKA) developments.

articleTitle: Low-RCS Transmitarray Using Phase Controllable Absorptive Frequency-Selective Structure
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: High gain antennas are important in many long-distance communication systems. Enlarging the radiating aperture is an effective approach to increasing the gain of an antenna. However, the increased scattering area will also result in a large radar cross section (RCS), which is often undesired for a lot of military systems. Therefore, it is critical to design a high-gain antenna with low out-of-band RCS signatures.

articleTitle: Nonlinear Inversion for Microwave Characterization of Targets in Non-Homogeneous Media
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Microwave inverse scattering in the presence of non-homogeneous media plays an important role in numerous applicative scenarios [1], [2]. Indeed, non-homogeneous media are present in several areas, such as in the industrial field for non-destructive testing or in civil engineering and geophysics, e.g., in the detection of buried structures. Moreover, other relevant applications can be found in cultural heritage monitoring, biomedical diagnostics and security applications [3], [4]. The main advantage of adopting microwave inverse scattering is that it allows inspecting and characterizing, in a non-invasive way, the targets and structures under test using safe and relatively cheap apparatuses.

articleTitle: Printed Directional Power Sensor
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Transmitted and reflected power is typically measured between the output of a power amplifier and the input of an antenna of a transmitter. Directional couplers in conjunction with power detectors are commonly used for this purpose, where the coupled port of the coupler is used to measure the transmitted power from the amplifier and the isolated port is used to measure the reflected power from the antenna. Classical directional couplers, such as quarter-wavelength coupled-line couplers, can become physically large components in a system, depending on the frequency of operation. A directional coupler also adds additional cost, power loss and generates excess heat.

articleTitle: Analytic and Numerical Aspects of the Nonsingular Laplacian Representation of the Asymptotic Part of the Layered-Medium Green Function in the Mixed Potential Formulation
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: We report on developments in the evaluation of matrix elements of the electric and magnetic field operators involving the asymptotic (large transverse wave-number or small transverse distances) components of the mixed-potential Green’s function of a layered medium. Subtracting these asymptotic terms significantly accelerates numerical computation of the Sommerfeld-type integrals required in constructing Green’s function and then the matrix elements [1].

articleTitle: Combined Spectral Methods to Study Complex Scattering Problems Formulated with the Wiener-Hopf Technique: the Semi-infinite Grounded Dielectric Slab problem
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In this work we present a new combination of spectral methods that allows to study complex scattering problem in spectral domain containing abrupt discontinuities of materials. The method is applied to a formulation of problem given in terms of incomplete Wiener-Hopf (WH) equations, where, for incompleteness, we intend that some of the physical boundary conditions arising from abrupt discontinuities provide terms in the WH equations not directly related to the plus and minus unknowns of the problem. This is the case of the semi-infinite grounded dielectric slab problem where the semi-infiniteness geometry of the material provide such situation. This problem is of great interest in antennas and propagation community and studies are proposed in different papers with different methods; see references in [1]. The WH incomplete equations are obtained as in [1] starting from the application of unilateral Laplace transform to wave equations defined in three different sub-regions, see Fig. 1.

articleTitle: A Unit Cell of Wideband Transmitarray Composed of Slots and Patches
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: A unit cell with slot-coupled patches is proposed that can be used for ultra-wideband transmitarrays. Its usefulness is verified by numerically.

articleTitle: Fast Alternating Direction Iterative Method for Poisson Equation of Potential
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: A fast alternating direction iterative (ADI) method is presented for solving Poisson equation of potential. The method has all right-hand sides (RHS) free of differential operator with the forcing function to be included in one step only. The derivation of Poisson equation is carried out based on Gauss’s law and Coulomb gauge for inhomogeneous media. The formulation of classical ADI method is also considered whereby the RHS still contain differential operators. Introducing the temporary auxiliary variable and manipulating the RHS terms lead to formulation of the fast ADI method. The computational efficiency is discussed in terms of flops count and memory requirement. Compared to the classical method, the fast ADI method has led to substantial flops count reduction and both methods require the same amount of memory space. Numerical results are illustrated with considerable simplification of each iteration using the fast ADI method having operator-free RHS.

articleTitle: On a Nature of ‘Real-Valued’ Resonances in Open Structures
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The key issue of the study is extension of the technique set forth in [1–3] to clarify and justify the nature of resonance phenomena observed for cylindrical open structures at real frequencies. When the plane electromagnetic wave diffraction by an open layered-dielectric scatterer possessing radial symmetry is considered and the corresponding boundary-value problem is solvable in cylindrical coordinates using separation of variables, the solution is represented as series in outgoing harmonics where the expansion coefficients are determined explicitly [1, 2] and in the form which enables one to calculate simultaneously the parameter sets when (i) a certain quantity of the principal expansion terms vanish and (ii) individual expansion coefficients have singularities (the latter yields resonances of the considered open structure). This fact paves the way to apply the analysis of multi-parameter Fourier series to the study of the scattered-field expansion coefficients and to determine the parameter values at which not only the partial invisibility and cloaking take place (caused by the suppression of the scattered-field harmonics), but also other well-known resonance phenomena.

articleTitle: Reducing SKA-LOW Station Calibration Errors by Wideband Gain Model Fitting
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Accurate calibration of the low-frequency aperture array stations of the Square Kilometre Array (SKA-LOW) is essential to achieve its ambitious science goals. Significant efforts have therefore been invested in characterising the response of the antennas within the station as well as the components of the analog receive paths between the antennas and digitisers resulting in experimentally validated models for the embedded element patterns (EEPs) and the receive path gains. In this contribution, these models are combined to build a realistic simulation of station calibration under the assumption that EEP variations can be ignored. It is found that fitting a simple gain model to the gain calibration solutions using weights proportional to frequency can reduce calibration errors to a level that permits over 99% beamformer efficiency. This suggests that wideband gain fitting is a powerful technique to improve robustness to errors in either the instrument or the source model used for calibration.

articleTitle: Fast Optimization Procedure for the Synthesis of Arbitrarily Conformable Magnetic Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In recent times, important research has been carried out within the wireless power transfer (WPT), due to the ever-increasing demand for contactless charging systems [1]. The inductive WPT is characterized by the rapid decay of near-field components. The magnetic field decays from the active coil proportionally to the cube of the distance from the passive receiver coil. Therefore, research in this sector has been oriented towards solutions that improve efficiency and working distance. Many solutions to enhance the performance of an inductive link have been presented in the literature. The three-coil system is probably one of the most common solutions, but at the same time efficient and compact. Instead of using just a driver circuit inductively coupled to a receiver (both resonating at the same frequency), an additional intermediate resonant passive coil is introduced. This transmit coil is strongly coupled to both the driver coil and the receiver. In this way, very small currents in the driver are enough to induce a large amount of current flowing into the transmitter.

articleTitle: Parametric Identification Method for Antenna Model on Time-Domain
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In general, the parameters of an antenna are described by their performance on the frequency-domain centred, in particular, at its band of operation. The reason lies mainly in the fact that the phasor form of the antenna fields, from which those parameters derive, are quite simple to handle from the mathematical perspective.

articleTitle: Improved implementation of wideband 90° hybrids
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Wideband micro wave 3 dB, 90° hybrids [1] are used to split signals equally between two outputs over a broad bandwidth with quadrature phasing independent of frequency. They are often also called symmetrical couplers, 90° directional couplers or quadrature couplers. Typical uses include microwave mixers, phase shifters, sinuous antennas, antenna feed networks, reflectometers and frequency discriminators. Approximately equiripple wideband performance can be achieved by cascading multiple coupled line sections with varying coupling coefficients. Numerous synthesis techniques exist to design a coupling profile for a desired frequency response. Continuously tapered coupling profiles typically have to be used at higher frequencies to overcome the performance degradation caused by the step discontinuities. 3 dB couplers are almost always implemented in a tandem configuration of two 8.34 dB couplers to overcome the requirement for very high coupling factors.

articleTitle: Stimulated Second Harmonic Emissions During Ionospheric Heating Experiments
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Stimulated Electromagnetic Emission (SEE) is secondary radiation produced during experiments involving the interaction of high power high frequency (HF) radio waves with the ionosphere. SEE has been developed into a useful remote sensing tool for the modified ionosphere with potential for aeronomy studies over the past four decades. Early experiments primarily considered emissions within a bandwidth of approximately 100 kHz of the pump (transmit) frequency ω<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>, so-called wideband SEE (WSEE), but work over the past decade has concentrated more on SEE within 100 Hz of the pump frequency, so-called narrowband SEE (NSEE). More recent investigations over the past few years carried out at the High Frequency Active Auroral Research facility (HAARP) in Alaska, have considered Second Harmonic Generation (SHG) in the narrowband SEE spectrum around twice the pump frequency 2ω<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>. This presentation will provide a review of the recent experimental observations of SHG at HAARP as well as some basic concepts of the nonlinear wave-wave processes that have been proposed to produce the observed SHG. A focus will be placed on the potential of SHG for diagnostic information during ionospheric heating experiments. It is useful to note that SHG has been developed into a useful diagnostic tool in the Laser Plasma Interaction (LPI) community since the 1970’s and this has attracted considerable interest in experiments, theory, and modeling. This knowledge base may possibly be applied to SHG observed during ionospheric heating experiments. However, for ionospheric interactions with high power radio waves, the earth’s magnetic field is found to play an important role in the spectral characteristics of the observed SHG spectrum as will be discussed in the presentation. As will be shown, the spectral lines are dependent on both the proximity of the pump frequency to a harmonic of the electron gyrofrequency Ω<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ce</inf> as well as the transmit antenna beam angle orientation relative the geomagnetic field. It will be shown that the SHG spectrum is easily as richly structured as the spectrum near the pump frequency as shown in Figure 1. These spectral lines are proposed to be produced by wave-wave interactions involving low frequency ion wave modes in the ionospheric plasma. These may include ion acoustic IA as well as ion Bernstein (IB) modes. The latter wave modes being ordered by the ion gyrofrequency Ω<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ci</inf> which is roughly 50Hz in the ionospheric interaction region. The correlation of the spectral lines at ω<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> and 2ω<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> as well as possible difference in the temporal evolution during heating underscores the importance of SHG as a potential important diagnostic tool during ionospheric heating experiments.

articleTitle: Fast frequency sweep using the Method of Moments: including the effect of the substrate
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: We propose an interpolation technique for the impedance matrix that accounts for the presence of the substrate. The method is based on the observation that, in the spectral domain, only a small part of the spectrum varies significantly with the frequency. Hence, it is possible to efficiently compute on-the-fly the rapidly varying part of the spectrum while interpolating the remainder. The proposed method is illustrated and validated through the example of a sphere above a layered substrate.

articleTitle: On the Mutual Coupling in an Active Highly Integrated TX Phased Array over Wide-Angle Scanning
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Communication at mmWave frequencies is currently being developed to achieve higher data-transfer capacity combined with a larger coverage in an energy-efficient way. Highly integrated TX phased array antennas have recently been proposed to improve the performance of such systems. The high-density integration results in an ultra-compact array system in which the knowledge of an accurate port-to-port mutual coupling and the associated power-transfer under operation is essential. The impact of the mutual coupling determines the quality of the overall system performance. This includes areas such as operation linearity, system efficiency, total output power, and the stability of the system. The investigated case has a non-standard impedance at each port of the antenna where an amplifier is directly integrated into the antenna elements in the array (direct-integration). Thus as a difference to passive antennas [1], a full multi-port electromagnetic-circuit co-simulation is required to characterize the system. Note that all ports need to be included, e.g. all the ports of the power amplifier, biasing, antenna for each element in the array. This increases the complexity of the system simulations due to the following facts: 1. the unit-cell consists of multi-ports with often unequal complex termination impedance, 2. active components are non-linear and their behavior depends on both the input power and the considered frequency. 3. although the transferred power to each port through mutual coupling is essential, the particular ports, like the input port of the amplifier, are more sensitive. 4. The transferred power depends on the scan angle of the array. This effect is similar to that of a passive antenna where the active-reflection coefficient depends on the scan-angle.

articleTitle: Fast Point Source Shadowing Determination for Mesh-Based Physical Optics Analysis
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Physical optics (PO) is a classic asymptotic method, for e.g. scattering analysis and antenna placement analysis. In the latter case point source illuminations are employed. This paper considers mesh-based PO, where the structure is meshed with large numbers of elements, typically triangles. A crucial step is to determine the geometric visibility of each mesh element/edge centroid. Not much has been published on methods yielding optimal runtime cost scaling for point source shadowing determination. This paper presents results with a new image-space buffer shadowing determination algorithm which relies on recursive multi-level subdivision of the source’s field-of-view. Optimal, linear runtime cost scaling is demonstrated for a very challenging test case.

articleTitle: Helical Resonator Notch Filter for Protection Against Jamming
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: A VHF/UHF band notch filter with helical resonators is developed to provide a deep notch with low loss in the pass-band of the filter. The traditional implementation of helical resonators is slightly altered to enable tuning opportunities in future designs. The helical resonators are coupled together using a non-standard coupling technique in order to provide a stopband response. The measured results show a notch depth of -81 dB at 260 MHz with the loss in the pass-band of -0.4 dB.

articleTitle: Efficient sensitivity analysis of EM structures using NLPLS-based PCE
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: This paper presents a Non-Linear Partial-Least-Squares-based Polynomial Chaos Expansion (NLPLS-based PCE) approach for high dimensional global sensitivity analysis. NLPLS-based PCE effectively reduces the system dimensionality using NLPLS and simultaneously extracts the statistical information on the same sample set, i.e. variance, using PCE. A post-processing step is applied to transform the NLPLS-based PCE surrogate to a standard PCE surrogate, described by the full set of system parameters. A variance-based global sensitivity analysis is then applied, quantifying each system parameter’s sensitivity as the partial influence on the total variance of the performance variable. This method is illustrated using a high-dimensional problem, namely, a 37-variable passive diplexer structure, requiring 30 analysis points to obtain a converged global sensitivity analysis. The diplexer is optimized for manufacturing and the fabricated diplexer performs as expected. Another 37-variable global sensitivity analysis is performed and compared to the original diplexer.

articleTitle: Snell Law for an Electromagnetic Pulse Travelling over a Torus Surface and Scattered by a Flat
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: We apply a new tool that is the Maxwell-Fredholm equations, to study the collision of an electromagnetic pulse with a flat surface of separation between the two parts of a torus-shaped artefact with a highly anisotropic refractive index that forces it to move over its surface. We find that it is possible to establish a relationship between the different angles involved depending on the parameters of the toroidal coordinates, which we call a particularization of Snell’s law.

articleTitle: Improved Hyperband Trifilar Coupled-line Balun for Impulse Radiating Antenna (IRA)
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: An improved hyperband trifilar coupled-line balun for an impulse radiating antenna (IRA) is presented in this paper. The trifilar balun is implemented in CST using the Finite Integration Technique (FIT) solver. The time domain result show well balanced excitation pulses for the IRA. From the frequency domain analysis of the balun, an amplitude balance within ±1.7 dB is attained with frequencies above 165 MHz and a phase balance within ±10° is realized between 300 MHz - 5 GHz of the frequency spectrum.

articleTitle: Ultra-Wide Band Frequency Selective Surface: design and experimental verification of performances for wide incident angle
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In the established UWB frequency range, for spatial filtering purposes a frequency selective surface is presented, simulated results showing a very large stopband between 1.78-14.32 GHz. Thus, strong polarization insensitivity is obtained with the structure and 45° angular stability for the pair: Transverse Magnetic (TM) and Transverse Electric (TE) incidence, respectively. Electromagnetic simulation was used to evaluate the performances of the structure, considering a 1.6 mm thick FR4 substrate with a 15 mm square-shaped unit cell edge. In an anechoic chamber, tests revealed an excellent match between simulation and experimental data, as well as proper device operation.

articleTitle: Rigorous Approach to the Calculation of Cut-off Wavenumbers in Waveguides with Multiple Embeddings
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: A perfectly electrically conducting (PEC) empty waveguide, of constant cross-section and axis aligned with the z-axis, supports time-harmonic propagating modes of the form u(x,y)e<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1ωt–iγz</sup>, where the function u satisfies the two-dimensional Helmholtz equation (Δ + λ)u = 0, k denoting wavenumber and λ=k<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>–γ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. Propagating modes occur at values of λ where non-trivial solutions of the Helmholtz equation occur; the cutoff wavenumber for each mode corresponds to setting γ to zero. If axially aligned PEC structures are inserted in the empty waveguide, the field distribution of each propagating mode is distorted and the corresponding propagation constant λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i</inf> is perturbed to a value λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i</inf> + △λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i</inf>. Some estimates of the perturbation △λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i</inf> obtained for particular structures are given in [1]. Accurate calculation of the perturbation to values of the propagation constants presents significant numerical challenges, particularly if the insert has sharp edges or comers, or is touching the inner boundary of the waveguide (or nearly so). Equally, accurate calculation of the modal field distribution is required in order to track its evolution from the empty waveguide mode as the size of the insert (or inserts) increases. In this context, any satisfactory method must provide cutoff wave numbers with any pre-specified accuracy and must be capable of resolving distinct modes in the spectrum even when their cutoff frequencies lie extremely close.

articleTitle: Artificial Neural Networks for Modeling of GaN Devices
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs) have asserted themselves as one of the most robust and multidimensional tools of the last decade [1]. Their usage is nearly ubiquitous and has improved the efficiency and overhead in achieving their intended goals than other methods. In the area of semiconductor device modeling, physics-based and empirical models have presented themselves as one of the most reliable methods used in academia and industry since their inception [2]. ANNs are quickly becoming a serious contender for being one of the viable options investigated by researchers [3].

articleTitle: Dual-Polarized Angle-Selective Surface Based on Two-Layer Frequency Selective Surface
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Angular selectivity of the electromagnetic (EM) waves, which allows EM waves of certain angles to transmit while blocking waves from other angles, is an important topic of modem electromagnetic engineering. The structure that can realize angular selectivity is named as angle-selective surface (ASS) or spatial filter. Among various applications, sidelobe reduction for antennas is desirable for many radar systems and can be potentially achieved by covering with a low-pass ASS.

articleTitle: Analysis of Random Cable Bundle Crosstalk Coupling Model Based on Hermite Interpolation Method
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In this article, a fast prediction method for statistical characteristics of cable bundle crosstalk, allowing accurate description of cable bundle crosstalk under nondeterministic geometric arrangement, is introduced. Different from the traditional flexible cable model, this method uses the Hermite interpolation method to simulate the spatial pose of the cable bundle according to the structural characteristics of the cable bundle in the actual situation. The condition of the Hermite interpolation method is the known node function value and the first derivative value, using random variables instead of known nodes, can be used to simulate the binding points in the cable bundle and the geometric uncertainty of the bundle. The Hermite interpolation formula under random node $\xi_{i}$ is as follows.

articleTitle: Diffraction by a Terminated, Semi-Infinite Parallel-Plate Waveguide with Four-Layer Material Loading: A Rigorous Wiener-Hopf Approach
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The analysis of electromagnetic scattering by open-ended metallic waveguide cavities is an important subject in the prediction and reduction of the radar cross section (RCS) of a target. This problem serves as a simple model of duct structures such as jet engine intakes of aircrafts and cracks occurring on surfaces of general complicated bodies. Some of the diffraction problems involving two- and three-dimensional cavities have been analyzed thus far based on high-frequency techniques and numerical methods. It appears, however, that the solutions due to these approaches are not uniformly valid for arbitrary dimensions of the cavity. Therefore it is desirable to overcome drawbacks of the previous works to obtain solutions which are uniformly valid in arbitrary cavity dimensions. The Wiener-Hopf technique is known as a powerful, rigorous approach for analyzing scattering and diffraction problems involving canonical geometries. In this paper, we shall consider a terminated, semi-infinite parallel-plate waveguide with four-layer material loading as an example of two-dimensional cavities, and analyze the plane wave diffraction rigorously using the Wiener-Hopf technique. Both E and H polarizations are considered.

articleTitle: Modulational instability and wave collapse of lower hybrid waves in the ionosphere and magnetosphere
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The modulational instability and collapse of lower-hybrid waves including both magnetosonic and lower-hybrid waves are investigated by analytical and numerical methods. The mechanism leading to the modulational instability is the nonlinear coupling of lower-hybrid waves with the much lower-frequency quasineutral density perturbations via the ponderomotive force described by the non-linear Schrodinger type equations. The result is a fllamentation of the high-frequency field producing elongated, cigar-shaped nonlinear wave packets aligned along the magnetic field with the plasma expelled outside (cavities). The analytical self-similar solution describing cavity collapse is described. We compared the results of numerical simulation for both 2D and 3D cavity geometries. We show that in three-dimensional solutions the transverse, with respect to the magnetic field, contraction remains prevailing.

articleTitle: The tunable single-/narrow-band terahertz metamaterial absorber through photoconductivity
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In this work, a photo-excited terahertz metamaterial absorber (PETMA) switched between single-band and narrow-band absorption is reported. Such an absorber includes three layers, which are a metal plate on the bottom, a dielectric layer, and a top unit attached to the dielectric substrate. Four corners of the square ring-shaped metallic resonator are embedded in photo-conducting semiconductors (silicon), respectively. Furthermore, the quadrate air columns (ACs) are inserted in the dielectric substrate to promote the absorption effect of this absorber. The simulations show that the proposed PETMA exhibits stable absorption performance at a wider incident angle.

articleTitle: Microwave Sub-Assemblies using Selective Laser Melting for Spaceflight
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Antenna systems using Additive Manufacturing (AM) has now been broadly accepted for space applications [1]. Using the geometric freedom offered by AM, LambdaG is commercializing 3D-printed antenna assemblies that enable high data-rate satellite downlinks and uplinks from low-earth orbit.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Reconstruction of the Magnetotail Configuration to Support Simulations of the Tearing Instability and Magnetic Reconnection
