publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Tearing instability is the main plasma mode responsible for the onset of magnetic reconnection in the Earth’s magnetotail, the key energy release process in the magnetosphere. Its free energy is provided by the mutual attraction of parallel current filaments in the tail current sheet while its dissipation is provided by the Landau resonance with electrons or ions resulting in the electron and ion tearing instabilities [1–2]. The major mystery for over forty years has been the nearly universal stability of the ion tearing mode [3], which was found unstable only for special magnetic flux distributions with accumulated flux regions and tailward gradients of the northward magnetic field component normal to the current sheet plane [4–5]. Otherwise, the tail must be squeezed to electron scales to release the magnetic energy [6]. To understand which of the scenarios works for the event of interest we apply the lazy learning algorithm of the k nearest neighbors (NN) to archives of spacebome magnetometer data from many missions over more than a quarter century [7]. NNs represent moments in the past that are closest to the event of interest in the state space formed by global indices of storm and substorm activity as well as the solar wind driving strength. A cloud of NNs in the state/input space produces a swarm of synthetic probes, of which only a few are the observations at the moment of interest. This swarm allows one to reconstruct the tail magnetic field with unprecedented details both before and after the reconnection onset [8]. We use this information to nudge the particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations of the magnetotail, as well as to compare the simulation results with the data-derived picture. The latter can also be used in global magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) simulations of the magnetosphere to supply them with the empirical resistivity maps derived from the reconstructed X-line distributions in the tail.

articleTitle: A Single-Cut Near-Field to Far-Field Transformation Using an Electrooptic Probe and a Robotic Arm at 300 GHz Band
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The Beyond 5 G technologies are emerging rapidly and the antenna characteristic measurements at 300 GHz band are required to support the technologies. At 300 GHz band, the measurement equipment is very expensive compared to the ones in the microwave range and very large compared to antennas. Tanaka et al. [1] have proposed the new inexpensive equipment using an electrooptic (EO) sensor and demonstrated the usefulness of the system in the planar near-field measurements for a horn antenna at 286 GHz.

articleTitle: On the Robustness of the Far Field in terms of Antenna Current variations
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Full-wave simulation of antennas together with fabrication and measurement of their electromagnetic properties are vital steps in the design of antennas. The complexity and cost of measurements push an increasing part of the design into the simulation domain. This is, in particular, true for highly-integrated arrays and antennas installed on large platforms, where direct measurements of all desired quantities are difficult or impossible. With the rapid development of high-quality electromagnetic simulation, it is nowadays accepted that well-conducted simulations and well-designed antennas closely agree for electromagnetic problems of reasonable electromagnetic size. Robustness and stability of electromagnetic quantities against small perturbations are vital in preserving simulation results into realization and measurements. This type of examination has a long history, with early results on shape-tolerances for the far-field behavior associated with radome antennas.

articleTitle: Extended Treatment of Statistical Moments of Random Fields in Nonlocal Markov Approximation
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: the paper extends the investigation of the non-local Markov approximation for statistical moments of the random fields, propagating in the extended stochastic medium. The problem is reduced to solving the appropriate ordinary differential equation. The explicit solution to the field spaced position coherence function is constructed.

articleTitle: Propagation of VLF Waves in the Magnetosphere from the DSX Spacecraft
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The Air Force Research Laboratory (AFRL) operated the Demonstration and Science Experiments (DSX) spacecraft in a 6000 x 12,000 km, 42° orbit for nearly two years spanning 2019-2021. Along with a suite of particle sensors, DSX carried a high-power very low frequency (VLF) transmitter and a sensitive receiver, both connected to an 80m dipole antenna. The system injected a variety of VLF waveforms into the inner magnetosphere to study wave propagation effects and interactions with relativistic trapped electrons.

articleTitle: The optics and feed design of the 18 metre reflector antenna for the ngVLA
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: A new radio astronomy interferometer called the Next Generation Very Large Array (ngVLA), a project of the National Radio Astronomy Observatory (NRAO), is envisaged to be built on the Plains of San Agustin in New Mexico, USA [1]. The instrument consists of offset Gregorian dual reflector antennas with approximately 244 antennas with an 18 meter aperture diameter and 19 antennas with 6 meter aperture diameter. At the reflector system’s focus is a suite of cryogenic feeds mounted on an indexer mechanism which cover the frequency range from 1.2 GHz to 116 GHz with a gap at the atmospheric absorption band between 50.5 GHz and 70 GHz.

articleTitle: On the Design of Matched Resistive n-Ports
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: This paper describes a straightforward design approach to the the design of resistive N-ports. Several examples are given for standard attenuator pads, symmetrical and also asymmetrical power dividers.

articleTitle: A Compendium of Exact Geometrical Optics Scattering by Two-Dimensional Metamaterial Structures
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The two-dimensional boundary-value problem of scattering by structures containing sharp edges allows for an exact geometrical optics (GO) solution only in particular cases, which usually involve restrictions on one or more of the following parameters: the number of plane incident waves; their polarization, phase and direction of incidence; the relationships between wavelength and dimensions of the scattering object; the electromagnetic properties of the scattering materials. An exact GO solution under incidence by a single plane wave is not known and presumably is not possible for wedge structures made of perfect electric or perfect magnetic materials [1], [2]. For penetrable wedges, the only known exact GO solution for a single wedge under incidence by a single plane wave is the scattering by a right-angle wedge made of anti-isorefractive DNG metamaterial [3]. The result obtained in [3] has been applied to obtain the exact GO scattering of two plane waves propagating in opposite directions by a DNG prism of rectangular cross section [4] and by DNG prisms of triangular cross sections [5]. An extension to polygonal cylinders whose cross-sections are regular pentagons or hexagons has been presented recently [6].

articleTitle: Modeling Common-Mode Currents in Auxiliary Structures of Motor-Drive Systems by a Multiconductor Transmission Line Approach
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Although increasing the switching frequency of variable speed drives provides higher efficiency and smaller size, the rapid changes in the states of the switches generate a common-mode (CM) voltage at the output of the inverter. The changes in the CM voltage result in CM currents. These CM currents are the source for problems such as bearing current, shaft voltage, and radiation from long cables [1]. Moreover, CM currents may cause electromagnetic interference within the surrounding environment [2]. These problems highlight the need for a method that can predict the CM current in all its flow paths.

articleTitle: A Case Study for Improving Performance of Frequency Selective Surface through Union of Sub-Sets and Particle Swarm Optimization
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Frequency Selective Surfaces (FSSs) consist of a repetition of a given pattern in a periodic way; typically, a dielectric substrate supports this arrangement giving rise to a two-dimensional array. Although relatively simple in structure, designing an FSS that exhibits large bandwidth and stable response to oblique incidence is not straightforward and requires special attention and significant computational effort. To address this problem, this study presents a methodology whereby an initial configuration of the FSS pattern is subjected to an optimization method for sizing the geometrical parameters. Consequently, the initial unit cell is first broken down into subsections, specifically as a “union of subsets”, then particle swarm optimization is used to achieve optimal design parameters that further improves the overall FSS performances. To validate the proposed method, an X-band FSS is proposed and optimized in a commercial simulation environment (Microwave Studio, Dassault Systèmes).

articleTitle: Array Antenna Solver Based on Macro Basis Functions, with Improved Accuracy
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In this work a macro basis function (MBF) scheme for method of moments (MoM) based array antenna analysis is discussed which allows for more flexibility in current variation. This is achieved by letting element-to-element far couplings be represented by MBF-to-MBF interactions, while letting antenna near-interactions be represented by the low-level basis functions. This is referred to as the semi-reduced formulation. It is shown that the semi-reduced approach is superior to a standard MBF reduced-system solution, when both are based on the same set of MBFs.

articleTitle: Toward non-metallic infrared metasurface filters with electrical and thermal controllability
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: A bicontrollable metasurface containing VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, a non-linear optical polymer, and teflon was simulated to function as a bandpass filter in the infrared spectral regime. The metasurface is a singly periodic array of identical unit cells composed of parallel rectangular VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> rods mounted on a silicon-dioxide substrate and covered with BAYI electro-optical polymer. The unit-cell dimensions are chosen such that the transmittance has a maximum in the 1418-to-l635-nm wavelength range, when the polymer face is normally illuminated by a plane wave with electric field parallel to the axis of the VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> rods. When the crystallographic phase of VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> is switched from monoclinc to tetragonal, the maximum transmittance redshifts from 1513 nm to 1656 nm, provided that no electrostatic field is present. However, when a dc potential of 50 V is applied across the polymer in the thickness direction, the minimum blueshifts from 1513 nm to 1418 nm at temperature $T\lt 58^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ temperature (VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> is monoclinic), and from 1656 nm to 1513 nm at $T\gt 72^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ temperature (VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> is tetragonal).

articleTitle: Hydrogen Intensity and Real time Analysis experiment: A radio interferometer for precision cosmology
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Hydrogen Intensity and Real time Analysis experiment (HIRAX) is an upcoming, compact radio interferometer used to detect the signature of baryonic acoustic oscillations (BAO) in auto-correlation using the red-shifted 21cm signal from 0.775 <z< 2.55. Currently, it is fully funded for a 256 element path-finder array (HIRAX256) at Swartfontein, close to the MeerKAT core, while the full array will comprise 1024 elements. Intensity mapping of the red-shifted 21 cm line will be carried out using HIRAX to provide highly competitive constraints on dark energy equation of state parameters, along with HI absorbers and radio transients. The advantage of intensity mapping in radio wavelengths over other wavelengths is that we obtain a detailed tomographic measurement of matter over large sky volumes. HIRAX will also provide complementary observations to eBOSS, DES, KiDS, Roman, Rubin and Euclid, as well as ground based CMB observations like ACTPol and Simons Observatory through cross-correlation estimates. In the radio wavelengths, it shares synergies with SKA MID’s intensity mapping surveys. Ancillary science goals of HIRAX include FRB detection and pulsar timing operations. To locate the detected FRBs, it is proposed to add out-trigger stations at various African partner countries to achieve resolutions ~ few milli-arc secs.

articleTitle: Exact Geometrical Optics Scattering by Truncated Metamaterial Cylinders
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The electromagnetic scattering of plane waves by penetrable structures with sharp edges can be obtained exactly as a geometrical optics solution only under certain conditions involving the shape and dimensions of the structure, the electromagnetic properties of the materials, and the number, direction of incidence, polarization, frequency and phase of the incident waves.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Discharge of the Pantograph Offline when the Contact Wire Is Covered with Ice
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The phenomenon of off-line discharge of the pantograph is greatly affected by the weather, especially when the contact net is covered by ice. Based on the generation mechanism of pantograph offline discharge, this paper establishes an equivalent circuit model of pantograph offline discharge when contact wire is icing, and calculates and analyzes its discharge voltage and current characteristics. First, verify the correctness of the built model by comparing the calculation results of the model with the measurement results; then apply the model to analyze the discharge conditions generated when the contact wire is covered with ice layers of different thicknesses. By comparing with the results of off-line discharge of pantograph under normal conditions, the influence of contact wire icing on the phenomenon of off-line discharge of pantograph and net is analyzed, and feasibility opinions are put forward for trains traveling through ice.

articleTitle: Optimization-Based Multimodal Characterization of Waveguide Transitions
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: A multimodal optimization technique is presented to determine the full multi-modal S-parameters for a three-port waveguide. The technique consists of measuring at one port only with a sliding short at one other port, and a short or perfect load at a third port. The reflection coefficient at the measured port is used to mathematically formulate the full set of S-parameters. An optimization algorithm is implemented to calculate the full set of S-parameters. The technique is demonstrated on a coaxial-rectangular waveguide transition with three propagating TE modes at frequencies up to 20 GHz.

articleTitle: A Retrospective of the SA-Mexico Bilateral Programme on Water Vapour Radiometry
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)

authors.preferredName: Miguel Velázquez de La Rosa Becerra

abstract: Water vapour radiometers (WVRs) are critical to management of radio astronomy sites and for surveying proposed future sites. We report on the outcomes of a South Africa – Mexico bilateral project on improving local capacity to design, maintain and operate WVRs in both countries. These include refurbishment of existing tipping radiometers at the Hartebeesthoek Radio Astronomy Observatory and the Large Millimeter Telescope, as well as the development of a new low-cost site surveying instrument. We further report on the development of a broadband multi-purpose K-Q band receiver and early installation efforts in Tulancingo, Mexico.

articleTitle: Synthesis of anisotropic twist-structure of nonorthogonal impedance stripes
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The problem of synthesizing an anisotropic plane implemented by a system of two frequent arrays of reactance stripes oriented relative to each other at an arbitrary angle is solved. The structure provides complete rereflection of a homogeneous plane incident wave to cross-polarization in a given (non-specular) direction. The expressions for the components of the reactance tensor and the angle of their orientation on the plane are obtained in an explicit form. It is shown that, in contrast to the structure of orthogonal stripes, in this structure, the orientation of non-orthogonal stripes turns out to be fixed on the entire anisotropic plane. In this case, the general impedance tensors of the structure of orthogonal stripes of variable orientation and the structure of non-orthogonal bands of fixed orientation take the same values. The results of numerical calculations are presented.

articleTitle: Antenna gain estimation using a millimeter-wave FMCW radar
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: We have developed a simple antenna gain estimation method using a millimeter-wave FMCW radar as a transmitting antenna from 77 GHz to 80 GHz. Our developed system consists of a millimeter-wave FMCW radar, a standard gain horn antenna as a calibrated reference antenna, a signal analyzer, and a W-band mixer.

articleTitle: Application of Parametric Fourier Series to the Analysis of Partial Invisibility and Resonance Scattering by Canonical Structures
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The method of parametric Fourier series is applied to the study of the scattered-field expansion coefficients. It is shown how to determine in the closed form the parameter sets at which partial invisibility and cloaking are possible for radial-symmetric layered-dielectric cylindrical structures, like a homogeneous dielectric rod or the Goubau line, caused by the elimination of several scattered-field harmonics.

articleTitle: Terahertz Wave Generation from DC Field-applied Hollow Air-plasmas
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Air-plasma is a powerful and convenient laboratory terahertz (THz) source that can be achieved by focusing a laser beam to ionize gaseous molecules in air. Nowadays, different attempts have been made to modulate the THz output of air-plasma, for instance, by using the dual-color laser pulses instead of the one-color scheme [1], by applying a DC-field on the air-plasma [2], or by shaping the spatial distribution of the air-plasma [3], Both the dual-color and DC-field-applied strategies contribute to greatly increase the THz output from air-plasma, due to the net electron currents accumulating under the laser actions.

articleTitle: Efficient simulation of 5G mobile base station antennas for RF safety analysis
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Existing fourth-generation (4G) cellular networks are currently being expanded with the deployment of fifth-generation (5G) technology. The introduction and use of higher frequency ranges in these deployments, e.g. millimetre wavebands, contributes to a significant increase in the number of mobile base stations. The primary benefits of 5G networks include increased data connections and improved service quality. Central to delivering these improvements to users is that 5G networks make use of advanced technologies, such as massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) antenna arrays.

articleTitle: Customizing the Response of Conformal and Low-frequency Magnetic Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In the last decades, metamaterials and metasurfaces has dramatically emerged as a fundamental research topic in electromagnetism due to the wide range of possible applications [1]. They have been proved useful for absorbing the undesired impinging e.m. energy and, thus, reducing an object radar cross section. Moreover, they can achieve exotic behavior, as negative refractive index, negative permeability and permittivity, and perfect lensing property. In the relatively low frequency regime (1-100 MHz), magnetic metasurfaces have become a powerful tool to enhance the performance of wireless power transfer devices as well as to increase the signal-to-noise ratio in MRI radiofrequency coils.

articleTitle: Design of Periodic Metamaterial Absorber for Terahertz Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Metamaterials which are also known as artificially engineered materials, are arranged periodically to display unique properties such as perfect absorption, perfect transmission which lead to enhanced performance in applications such as sensing, absorption, imaging, etc. Terahertz frequency is in the region of the electromagnetic spectrum between microwave and infrared bands where natural materials rarely interact with the waves within that frequency range. Terahertz (THz) metamaterial-based sensors have been recently developed by utilizing their pseudo-surface plasma effects to enhance the electric field of the incident THz waves [1]. This phenomenon improves the quality of the measured signals [2]. Metamaterial characteristics can be obtained using split-ring resonators, fishnets, etc. and used to design THz devices such as modulators, antennas, filters, and absorbers. THz metamaterial absorbers gained more attention as they can absorb THz waves almost uniformly which make them most suitable for sensing application. Replacing metals in the multilayer metamaterial structure with the semiconductors increases the design flexibility while still having the negative permittivity to keep the metamaterial properties intact. Permittivity of semiconductors can be improved by varying temperature, light intensity, applied voltage and external magnetic fields [3–5]. Therefore, THz metamaterial with semiconductor achieves reconfigurability which is critical for several applications.

articleTitle: Aspects of the Feed Production and Support for MeerKAT and SKA – a Retrospective View
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: This paper highlights some of the lessons learned during the design, production, and operation of the MeerKAT and SKA feeds and the design of the reflector surfaces.

articleTitle: Chequered-Network Compressive Arrays: Overview and Future Directions
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Beamforming controls in antenna arrays, whether transmitters, receivers, variable amplifiers or phase shifters, are expensive compared to the rest of the array hardware. Subarrays combine antenna elements to simplify the system in some way, such as reducing the number of beamforming controls or assigning a particular beam direction to each subarray. Subarrays can each comprise a dedicated subsection of a larger array or can share parts of the array. Completely overlapped subarrays share the entire array aperture, offering the finest control over the radiation patterns. With the other subarrays terminated in matched loads, each subarray can be characterised as a conventional array. In the $M \times N$ complex-valued feed-network response matrix $\Phi$, the rows contain the N antenna-element excitations for each of the M subarrays. Conventional wisdom is that hardware constraints dictate the design of feed networks, but chequered-network compressive arrays allow the implementation of arbitrary feed networks, with the elements of $\Phi$ specified independently [1, 2]. This capability allows antenna arrays to be designed primarily on the basis of the pattern requirements with the effects of hardware constraints being significantly reduced. This flexibility enables rapid, application-driven development with full control over the array patterns, and the implementation of antenna-array configurations that could not previously be considered.

articleTitle: Multi-scale behavior of Langmuir turbulence during ionospheric heating experiments
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: We present new results of multi-scale simulations of Langmuir turbulence during heating experiments where a powerful electromagnetic wave is injected into the overhead ionosphere where it excites parametric instabilities leading to turbulence on multiple spatial and temporal scales. The simulations are carried out using a generalized Zakharov model [1, 2] in which the complex phase and amplitude of the high-frequency electromagnetic and electrostatic waves are solved using an implicit method, and are coupled to ion fluctuations via the ponderomotive force acting on the electrons, which pull the ions via the space charge electric field. The 3-wave parametric decay instability (PDI) and 4-wave oscillating two-stream instability (OTSI) lead to strong Langmuir turbulence with nucleation and burn-out cycles of localized Langmuir wave packets trapped in ion density cavities.

articleTitle: Application of Capsule Networks to Open-set Target Recognition of ISAR Images of Small Complex Targets
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The rising popularity of small aircraft such as multi-rotor drones, and the security concerns linked to small aircraft create an increasing demand for systems that are able to detect and recognize such targets. An effective target recognition system should be able to recognize targets in a real-world setting, under conditions where the system receives noisy inputs. In addition to being able to handle noisy inputs, a target recognition system should be able to handle both known targets (targets that it has been trained on) and unknown targets (targets that do not form part of the training set). Open-set classification such as this is non-trivial, as it can be a challenging task to train a machine learning model to recognize inputs that do not belong to any class observed in training.

articleTitle: Radar Cross Section Analysis of a Finite Parallel-Plate Waveguide with Four-Layer Material Loading: A Rigorous Wiener-Hopf Approach
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The analysis of electromagnetic scattering by open-ended metallic waveguide cavities is an important subject in the prediction and reduction of the radar cross section (RCS) of a target. This problem serves as a simple model of duct structures such as jet engine intakes of aircrafts and cracks occurring on surfaces of general complicated bodies. Some of the diffraction problems involving two-and three-dimensional cavities have been analyzed thus far based on high-frequency techniques and numerical methods. It appears, however, that the solutions due to these approaches are not uniformly valid for arbitrary dimensions of the cavity. Therefore it is desirable to overcome drawbacks of the previous works to obtain solutions which are uniformly valid in arbitrary cavity dimensions. The Wiener-Hopf technique is known as a powerful, rigorous approach for analyzing scattering and diffraction problems involving canonical geometries. In this paper, we shall consider a finite parallel-plate waveguide with four-layer material loading as a geometry that can form cavities, and analyze the plane wave diffraction rigorously using the Wiener-Hopf technique. Both E and H polarizations are considered.

articleTitle: A Broadband Wide Field-of-view True-time delay-based Multi-Beamforming Architecutre and Design
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: To realize the combinations of wide field-of-view (FoV) and multi-beamforming capability with an affordable implementation as required by SKA mid-frequency dense array, this paper presents a broadband wide field-of-view true time-delay based multi-beamforming architecture guided by the concept of allocating beams over the full FoV. The system is designed as a two-dimensional silicon-based beamformer combined with a chessboard beam-selector and is able to produce 16 independent beams covering ±45° scanning angle while maintaining a flexible digital multi-beamforming capability within the full optical FoV. Thus the design provides a feasible solution that fulfills the wide FoV, flexible multi-beamforming and cost-effective system design requirements for large-scale dense array.

articleTitle: Design of 3 mm Frequency Band SiGe BiCMOS Power Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: This paper presents a 3mm frequency band power amplifier based on the technology of SiGe BiCMOS. A fully differential structure consisting of cascode was adopted, and transformer match was used to achieve good performance and save areas. Measured peak gain is 4.7 dB at 101 GHz, with a 3 dB bandwidth of 23 GHz from 87 GHz to 110 GHz. The input and output return losses are less than -7.4 dB and -7.6 dB, respectively. The isolation is less than -27.4 dB in the 3 dB bandwidth range. The simulated result of output 1dB compression point power is 5.1 dBm at 94 GHz. The chip size is 1.15 mm×0.7 mm (including input and output test baluns and pads), which can be applied to radar, communication, imaging and other fields.

articleTitle: Design and Verification of a Hybrid Multi-Beamforming system for SKA MFAA
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: A broadband hybrid muti-beamforming system applicable to SKA Mid-Frequency Aperture Array is presented in this paper. The hybrid beamforming system adopts a two-stage architecture that combines analog and digital beamforming. The analogue beamforming subsystem is able to provide a 16-element tile with 2~16 simultaneous beams covering ±45° spatial area and a flexible beam-selection capability by using a true-time delay and chessboard switching structure. The second-stage beamforming then produces beams in a full digital way within each input analog beam by CTPM that implements analog to digital converting, channelizer and digital beamforming.

articleTitle: Nonlinear interaction between Alfvén waves and drift-wave instabilities in LAPD
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The Basic Plasma Science Facility (BaPSF) at UCLA is a US national user facility for studies of fundamental processes in magnetized plasmas. The centerpiece of the facility is the Large Plasma Device (LAPD), a 20m long, magnetized linear plasma device <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>. LAPD has been utilized to study a number of fundamental processes, including: collisionless shocks <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, dispersion and damping of kinetic and inertial Alfvén waves <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, compressional Alfvén waves for ion-cyclotron range of frequencies heating <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup>, flux ropes and magnetic reconnection <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sup>, three-wave interactions and parametric instabilities of Alfvén waves <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6, 7</sup>, turbulence and transport <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</sup> and interactions of energetic ions and electrons with plasma waves <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">9</sup>.

articleTitle: New Formulation Of Physical Optics Approximation For Edge Diffraction By Dielectric Wedges
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In this study, edge diffraction of an electromagnetic plane wave by a two-dimensional dielectric wedge has been analyzed based on the physical optics (PO) approximation. The exterior and interior radiation fields of dielectric wedges may be derived from equivalent electric and magnetic currents, which can be determined by geometrical optics (GO) rays. A modified formulation of PO has been proposed to improve the limitation of PO solution. The modification is inherited from the conducting wedge case [1], in which the formulation of diffracted field can mend the error of PO to satisfy the boundary condition at the wedge surface. This solution is obtained by adding the concept of hidden rays [2], and changing the angular period of cotangent functions of diffraction coefficient based on edge condition at the wedge tip.

articleTitle: A joint magnetoelectric sensor and human head model for biomagnetic simulation
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In recent years, thin-film magnetoelectric (ME) magnetic-field sensors have emerged as novel and advantageous devices for biomagnetic measurements. These ME sensors promise contactless readings of the magnetic fields generated by the human body, e.g., in magnetocardiography, with added benefits such as operation at room temperature without magnetic shielding [1]. The ME sensors considered here are based on strain-coupled thin-film magnetostrictive and piezoelectric layers on a cantilever. An incident magnetic field deforms the magnetostrictive layer which is coupled to a deformation of the piezoelectric layer giving a voltage signal. Previous studies often characterize the sensor performance under simplified homogeneous magnetic-field conditions. We have demonstrated that these sensors show a significantly different behavior under inhomogeneous magnetic-field excitation [2]. Here, we discuss a multiscale simulation approach using a joint sensor and simplified human head model for evaluation of sensor performance at different positions and orientations.

articleTitle: The South African Maritime Domain Awareness Satellite Constellation and Beyond
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: MDASat is the Cape Peninsula University’s (CPUT’s) third satellite mission, following on ZACUBE-I’s (TshepisoSat) and ZACUBE-2’s successful development, launch and operation. The mission objectives of ZACUBE-2 were re-aligned and augmented to allow the satellite to function as a precursor mission for the Operation Phakisa “MDASat” constellation, as mandated by the Department of Science and Technology (DST). Operation Phakisa, a fast-track implementation of the South African National Development Plan, focuses on the key areas of ocean economy and marine security. With the expansion of South African waters, a special need is emerging for effective Maritime Domain Awareness (MDA).

articleTitle: Diffraction by a Semi-Infinite Plate with Fractional Boundary Conditions
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The analysis of the scattering by materials with fractional boundary conditions (FBC) [1] is an important subject in electromagnetic theory and antenna design studies. Recently, the studies of the artificial magnetic conductor (AMC) surfaces have been attracting a lot of attention. Fractional boundary conditions (FBC) show intermediate scattering properties between perfect electric conductor (PEC) and perfect magnetic conductor (PMC). ‘Fractional’ means fractional derivative [2] of the total electric field components in this paper. The surfaces with FBC have scattering characteristics close to the AMC surfaces since the reflection phase of the surfaces with FBC becomes controllable by shifting the fractional order.

articleTitle: Effect and behavior of lightning on composite material structures used in aircraft
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: This project focuses on performing computer simulations to estimate the effects of lightning on aircrafts and its interference in the on-board electronic systems. Models composed of aluminum alloys and carbon fiber composite materials were implemented. From the simulations performed in the CST Studio software, it was possible to observe the influence of several factors on the electric current behavior. The way fibers are organized in the matrix structure, the fiber presence proportion and the area where the affected composite material is located on the aircraft.

articleTitle: Some trends and problems in algebraic preconditioning for solving dense method of moments linear systems
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: We present computational techniques based on the class of preconditioned Krylov subspace methods that enable to carry out large-scale simulations of Computational Electromagnetics problems modeled via integral equations. This analysis requires the solution of very large, typically dense, linear systems that cannot be afforded by conventional direct methods. For example, accurate modeling of a perfectly conducting sphere of diameter of 1,800 wavelengths yields systems with more than 3 billion equations. For many integral formulations of practical interest, the convergence of Krylov subspace methods is often slow and needs to be accelerated by a technique called preconditioning, which transforms the initial system into an equivalent one that has more favorable eigenvalues distribution, i.e., most of the eigenvalues are grouped close to point one of the spectra. An effective preconditioner should be cheap to compute, easy to combine with the data structure of fast integral equations solvers, so that it can maintain an overall O(n log n) complexity in both time and space, and scale satisfactorily with the frequency of the problem and the number of processors, delivering fast convergence on a wide range of geometries and physical parameters. These requirements are often in contradiction with each other.

articleTitle: Novel Integral Equation Formulation for Scattering on Dielectric Objects Free of Low-Frequency and Oversampling Breakdowns
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In our recent work [1] we have demonstrated analytic solution of a novel Surface-Volume-Surface Electric Field Integral Equation with magnetic current (SVS-EFIE-M formulation) for the problem of Hertzian dipole radiation in the vicinity of a homogeneous non-magnetic dielectric sphere. The SVS-EFIE-M stated with respect to magnetic current $\hat{n}\times I$ on object’s surface S is shown in (1), where $\overline{\overline{G}}_{m\in}$ is the magnetic field dyadic Green’s function of the homogeneous non-magnetic space with relative permittivity $\epsilon, \overline{\overline{G}}_{e0}$ is the electric field dyadic Green’s function of free-space, and $\hat{n}\times E^{inc}$ is the tangential component of the incident electric field on the surface S. It is obtained through single-source magnetic current based surface integral representation of the electric field inside the dielectric object (see first term in (1) representing $\hat{n}\times E, E$ being the total electric field) constrained by the classical Volume-EFIE (V-EFIE) enforced on the boundary of the object for the tangential component of the electric field.

articleTitle: Design of High-Gain Lens Antenna Using Pixelated Phase Gradient Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In this paper a novel systematic design method based on Genetic Algorithm (GA) for transmitting lens antenna design is introduced. The antenna consists of a dual-layer phase-gradient metasurface (PGMS). GA has been used to design the unit cells configurations incorporating in the cost function the performances of the main parameters of an antenna such as gain, bandwidth and side lobe level. To design a set of pixilation-based unit cells, a single bit with a binary value of 0 or 1 that indicates the presence or absence of copper at the pixel level, respectively, has been considered for each pixel. By setting the dimensions of each unit cell with a value of 0.4$\lambda\times 0.4\lambda$ ($\lambda$ being the wavelength at 12 GHz) and with binary optimization based on GA, appropriate transmission coefficient with suitable transmission phase in the range of [0,2$\pi$] has been achieved. The proposed PGMS antenna uses a 1.58 mm thick, RO4003C (lossy) transmission lens with a dimension of $110\times 110\times 35mm^{3}$ and a microstrip patch antenna acts as a radiation source. The proposed PGMS antenna has a 20.3 dB realized gain which is 13.5 dB greater than the single patch antenna one (6.8dB) and exhibits -15.5dB side lobe level (SLL) at 12 GHz. Simulation results of the proposed PGMS antenna verify the validity of the design method.

articleTitle: Design of W-band On-chip Differential Cross-coupled Gysel Power Combiner
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Based on the 0.13 μm SiGe BiCMOS process, a W-band On-chip differential Gysel power combiner is designed. A fully differential cross-coupled structure is used and electromagnetic simulation is performed using a 3D electromagnetic field simulation software. The simulation results show that in the 90-100GHz design frequency band, All ports are well-matched, the input reflection coefficient S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> is less than -15.6dB and S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">22</inf> is less than -15.7dB and the output reflection coefficient S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">33</inf> is less than -15.6dB. The insertion loss S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">31</inf> and S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">32</inf> are both less than 4dB. The amplitude unbalance of two input ports is less than 0.03dB and the phase unbalance of the two input ports is less than 0.4°. At the same time, the combiner can also be used as a power. The chip core size is 814um × 205um (not including input and output test balun and pads), which can be applied to power distribution in phased array system.

articleTitle: Efficient Broadband Modeling of Microwave Devices with Machine Learning and Analytical Extension of Eigenvalues
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Accurate modeling of the broadband behavior of RF and microwave devices is of great interest as it can facilitate design optimization and high-level simulation. Machine learning (ML) techniques, in particular neural networks (NN), have recently gained recognition as a powerful tool for this purpose. Once trained, NNs can serve as an alternative to conventional methods such as full-wave simulations, which can be computationally expensive, or empirical models, which can have limited ranges of validity and accuracy. On the other hand, traditional NN-based modeling requires a large amount of training data and tends to have drastically worse performance on out-of-domain inputs. This coupled with the high computational cost for obtaining training data, severely hinders the application of NNs in device modeling.

articleTitle: A Tri-Ridge Flared Horn Reflector Antenna Feed for Radio Astronomy
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Tri-ridge waveguides (TRWs) have been shown to have wider single-mode bandwidth when compared to quad-ridged waveguides (QRWs) [1], which presents an opportunity for the design and optimization of Tri-Ridge Flared Horns (TRFHs) to compete against the widely accepted Quad-Ridge Flared Horns (QRFHs) as reflector feeds in radio astronomy. Fig. 1 shows an example of a TRFH design, showing the 120° separation of the ridges. This talk will present design methods and initial results for the performance of a TRFH as a wideband reflector feed. Specific attention will be given to the design of the horn and ridge tapers to guarantee trapped-mode free operation, as well as provide controlled wideband radiation and impedance performance. Discussion of the three-way digital orthogonal-mode transducer as well as the details of the optimization method (with a goal of maximum receiving sensitivity over a nominally 3.5:1 bandwidth) will be provided.

articleTitle: Design of an 8×8 parallel-fed mm-wave microstrip antenna array for wireless power transmission
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The development and application of wireless power transmission have attracted extensive attention of researchers. In order to meet the design requirements of system miniaturization and power directional transmission, this paper proposes an 8×8 parallel-fed mm-wave microstrip antenna array operating in the W-band. The simulation results show that the -10dB bandwidth of the antenna array is about 5.5GHz, from 90.5 GHz to 96GHz. In this frequency range, the VSWR is below 2 and the gain is greater than 22dBi. The peak gain is 24dBi and the half-power beamwidth is about 8° at 94GHz.

articleTitle: Computing Gabor Coefficients for a Scattering Problem: Super Exponential Converging Accuracy and a more Localized Representation
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Optical scatterometry is a non-destructive inspection technique to evaluate possible production deformations for integrated circuits. A key component of optical scatterometry is a Maxwell solver to obtain accurate information regarding the electromagnetic scattering from the structures of interest. This Maxwell solver also needs to be capable to quickly adapt the geometrical details of these structures to take various possible deformities into consideration for the fast computation of electromagnetic scattering. A fitting Maxwell solver [1] takes the form of a spatial-spectral domain integral equation such that its computational domain is comparable to the volume of the scattering objects of interest, e.g. parts of an integrated circuit. The spatial-spectral representation in terms of Gabor frames allows to analytically and efficiently incorporate the response of a planarly layered background medium, since the setting of optical scatterometry for integrated circuits is characterized by such a background description. The Gabor frames as in [1] make it possible to describe the electromagnetic fields and scattering objects as weighted sums of shifted and modulated Gaussian window functions, where the so-called Gabor coefficients are the weighting coefficients. We want to make more efficient use of the Gabor frames, which requires the computation of Gabor coefficients, such that the Maxwell solver [1] becomes faster and more suitable for optical scatterometry applications.

articleTitle: A demonstration of multiplicative tapering in FDTD Green’s function diakoptics
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: We have implemented a simulation tool for finite difference time domain (FDTD), or lattice Green’s function (LGF) diakoptics. This amounts to fully self-consistent FDTD boundary conditions for possibly disjoint computational domains. Our main focus is the multiplicative tapering of the LGFs, which results in a crucial reduction in computational and storage costs, and thus ensures the viability of LGF diakoptics. We show that a simple truncation is not sufficient. Instead we show the effectiveness of using a Hann window for both a homogeneous setup and a configuration with a large dielectric contrast.

articleTitle: Wave-Particle Interactions in Earth Outer Radiation Zone
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Recent space flight missions have demonstrated through in situ observations that electrons from hundreds of kilovolts to energies over 10 megaelectron volts (MeV) can be produced within the Earth’s outer radiation belt on timescales as short as a few minutes. Such rapid acceleration is the result of low-energy populations of electrons (tens to hundreds of keV in energy) interacting with electromagnetic waves in the lower band whistler-mode chorus frequency range. MMS (Magnetospheric Multiscale) mission data show that source electrons (in a typical energy range of one to a few tens of keV energy) produced during magnetospheric substorms play a central role in amplifying the chorus waves in the magnetosphere (Baker et al., 2019). Chorus waves rapidly heat and accelerate the lower energy electrons up to relativistic energies. Geomagnetic activity driven by strong solar forcing almost invariably leads to ultra-relativistic electron production through the intervening step of wave interactions during intense substorms (Baker et al., 2019). We have been able to explore wave-particle interactions in essentially all parts of the Earth’s space environment using recent particle and wave sensing experiments. The ability to carry out such investigations without the interference of confining chamber walls makes near-Earth space a nearly ideal plasma physics laboratory. Well-instrumented space missions such as the Van Allen Probes dual-satellite pair and the four-spacecraft MMS constellation have greatly improved our understanding of particle acceleration processes. We have confirmed in detail that wave-particle interactions are of key importance over a broad range of energies and in virtually all regions of the magnetosphere. This presentation provides a summary of the wide variety of the wave-particle interactions that have been examined with the MMS and Van Allen Probes spacecraft missions. We present case studies of electron acceleration events observed with these missions with emphasis on the great storms of 2017-2019 that have not had close attention in prior studies. We also examine in some detail local losses of magnetospheric particles due to intense wave-particle scattering interactions. This latter topic has not had the attention deserved for such an important theme.

articleTitle: Full-wave analysis of mutual coupling in the HIRAX radio telescope
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The Hydrogen Intensity and Real-time Analysis experiment (HIRAX [1]) isa radio telescope which will consist of 1000 6m-wide, closely-packed and orientable dishes operating between 400 and 800 MHz. The experiment aims to indirectly constrain the properties of cosmological quantities, such as Dark Energy, by measuring the hydrogen intensity delay power spectrum and extracting the Baryon Acoustic Oscillations (BAO) feature. The principle is to separate between the cosmological (BAO) information residing at high delay k<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">‖</inf>-modes and the foreground signal residing at low delays. However, as is the case for other similar telescopes [2], mutual coupling between neighboring, but also far-apart, antennas can cause the foreground signal to contaminate high delay modes thereby reducing the detection window of the cosmological signal.

articleTitle: Faster Optimization of Quadruple-Ridged Flared Horns Using Geometric Feasibility Parameters
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The design of a quadruple-ridged flared horn (QRFH) is onerous due to the large geometric (or optimisation) parameter space that defines the shape of the horn, and the lengthy computation times in evaluating the horn’s performance. The QRFH typically performs over a very wide frequency range, and over this range, it needs to be finely evaluated to ensure that no unwanted frequency aberrations or trapped modes occur. The electromagnetic (EM) computation times are large not only in determining the horn’s performance but also in evaluating the horn’s performance on a reflector system, which is typically electrically large, as would generally be the case for radio astronomy receivers. The primary performance metric for the system is receiving sensitivity or G/T, which requires that the antenna temperature be calculated from the reflector system radiation pattern on a finely sampled full sphere. This is, of course, computationally very expensive on electrically large systems, but accurate approximation techniques exist [1].

articleTitle: Where RF meets DC
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Stepped-impedance stripline in DC feed ciruits are excellent candidates for distributing DC supply voltage in printed circuit boards. They can provide very low port impedances over wide bandwidths and eliminate feedback and coupling paths via the DC feed circuitry.

articleTitle: The ngVLA: A technical development update
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The National Radio Astronomy Observatory (NRAO) has engaged the broad scientific and technical communities in the design of a next-generation Very Large Array (ngVLA), a large-scale research infrastructure project under development for the National Science Foundation Astronomical Sciences Division (NSF-AST) through a cooperative agreement with Associated Universities, Inc. The ngVLA is an interferometric array with ten times greater sensitivity and spatial resolution than the current VLA and ALMA, operating in the frequency range of 1. 2-116 GHz.

articleTitle: Numerical Errors Reduction in Transient Simulations with Resistor Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: It has been investigated about the best parameters to simulate transmission lines using a simple numeric model and taking into consideration the stability and numeric precision. In this study, two-phase lines have been used as examples for the application of the proposed model. It has been used phase-mode transformations to simplify the line modeling and two-phase lines have been represented by two independent mode lines. These independent transmission lines can be represented by cascade of circuits with concentrated elements and this representation has been solved using the trapezoidal rule. In previous applications of this association of the mentioned simple model and the trapezoidal rule, it has been detected undesirable oscillations and numeric error when classic cascade $\pi$-circuits or T-circuits are applied. Searching for highly reducing these numeric problems and reducing the computational time in transient simulations, damping resistors and sparse matrix techniques are applied. In case of this paper, two different types of damping resistors will be presented. One of these damping resistors is inserted in parallel to the elements that represent longitudinal line parameters. The other damping resistor type is inserted in series to the elements that represent the transversal line parameters.

articleTitle: Scattering Analysis of Thick Wires with the MoM using Macro Basis Functions
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: This work is concerned with the analysis of scattering by conducting wires connected to conducting structures, using the method of moments (MoM). Based on thin-wire assumptions, low numbers of degrees of freedom (DoFs) are required by typical exact-kernel thin-wire MoM solvers, for accurate analysis. However, the thin-wire assumptions break down when the wire diameter becomes appreciably large in terms of the wavelength. An approach based on macro basis functions (MBFs) for wire current representation is outlined, aimed at extending the wire thickness range of accurate analysis, while maintaining a low number of DoFs similar to that of thin-wire formulations. Preliminary results demonstrate the effectiveness of the MBF approach.

articleTitle: Towards Cost-effective EMC Strategies for Nanosatellites in Africa
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The African space arena has rapidly transformed over the past 25 years with the increased use of small satellites. Of the 40 African satellites in space as at the end of 2020, more than half were launched during the last 5 years up to that point in time [1]. The trend is set to continue, with the African Space Policy geared towards social, political, and economic integration in space science and technology, utilizing nanosatellite technology [2]. Priority areas include earth observations, remote sensing, and satellite telecommunications [3].

articleTitle: Transverse Components of the Transverse-Magnetic Field in a Waveguide with Nonstationary and Inhomogeneous Magnetodielectric Filling
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In this paper we consider the propagation of transverse-magnetic (TM) (H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Z</inf>=0, $E_{Z}\neq$0) electromagnetic waves in an ideal regular waveguide of arbitrary cross section. It is assumed that the permittivity and permeability of the magnetodielectric filling of the waveguide are functions of the coordinate and time ($\varepsilon$(z, t), $\mu$(z, t)). From the system of Maxwell equations, the wave equation for the longitudinal component of the electric vector is obtained, with help of which the transverse-magnetic field in the waveguide is described. From the system of Maxwell equations are also found the analytical expressions for the transverse components of the magnetic and electric vectors of the transverse-magnetic field in the waveguide. They are expressed in terms of the longitudinal component E<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Z</inf>(x,y,z,t) of the electric vector.

articleTitle: Initial Results for Cross-Polarisation Jamming of Monopulse Radar
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Cross-polarisation jamming aims to induce an angular error in a tracking radar by using the polarisation orthogonal to the radar’s primary polarisation. While general statements about the many challenges associated with cross-polarisation jamming abound, little or no detail is provided. This study evaluates the performance of a cross-polarisation jammer against to monopulse antennas in an effort to start addressing this lack of detailed information. Initial results demonstrate that significant distortion of the monopulse ratios occur even when no significant tracking error is achieved. This outcome suggests that further study of cross-polarisation jamming is required.

articleTitle: PCB Based High Power L-Band Duplexer
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The design of a high power PCB based L-band Duplexer is presented. A new PIN diode PCB based mounting method is described. Measurements of the Duplexer’s small signal and high power operation is given.

articleTitle: Analysis of Electromagnetic Disturbance Characteristics of Traction Drive System
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The traction rotating system, especially its main components rectifier and inverter, generates electromagnetic disturbance, which affect the normal operation of on-board equipment greatly. In this paper, the mechanism of electromagnetic disturbance of traction converter is studied, the control logic and circuit model are jointly simulated using Simplorer, the traction converter model is established, and the radiation characteristics of the output cable are analyzed with this model. This article provides an effective theoretical basis and decision support for the electromagnetic compatibility risk assessment of high-speed rail signal on-board equipment.

articleTitle: Accurate and efficient modeling of gain patterns of multiband pixelated antenna by deep neural networks
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Pixelated microstrip antennas present considerable versatility to antenna designers in that their geometries can assume a great variety of shapes and sizes. The design process however usually entails significant computational expense, as evolutionary algorithms in conjunction with direct full-wave simulations need to be used in order to discover an optimal antenna geometry that would best yield the desired performance characteristics – e.g. thousands of full-wave simulations of candidate geometries may be required before this objective is attained. This suggests the need for computationally inexpensive machine-learning-based models that can be used as surrogates for the full-wave simulations.

articleTitle: Computing Surface Integral Equation Matrices with Shared Memory Parallelization
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: An efficient shared memory parallelization strategy is presented for computing matrices resulting from surface integral equation based methods in time-harmonic electromagnetics (EM). In the numerical solution of EM problems with methods such as the method of moments (MoM) a significant portion of the solution time is dedicated to filling dense interaction matrices. Developing efficient parallelization strategies to take advantage of all of the available computational resources of multi-core central processing units (CPU) is thus critical in the fast solution of computationally demanding EM problems. The proposed scheme is applied to the electric field integral equation (EFIE)-based MoM and shown to demonstrate good parallel efficiency.

articleTitle: Orthogonal Polarization Conversion Reflectarray Using L-shape Elements
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In recent years, many studies have been made on reflectarrays in which an incident wave is reflected by cross polarization. For example, the reflector using two V-shaped elements [1] and the reflecting plate [2] using a genetic algorithm (GA) have been proposed. However, it is difficult to obtain phase shift in the range of 360° accompanying with the orthogonal polarization conversion for reflectarray antennas. We also have proposed a reflected plate with simple-shaped unit element in which an oblique straight line is stepped [3]. Although these elements realize an arbitrary phase, a good amplitude characteristic has not been produced.

articleTitle: A Figure of Merit for the X-Band All-Sky Survey
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The X-Band All-Sky Survey (X-BASS) is a single-dish experiment aimed at mapping the sky in the frequency range 7–15 GHz. When designing such a system, one must rely on various figures of merit (FoMs) to describe its performance. With the main goal of X-BASS being to aid observations of the cosmic microwave background (CMB) anisotropy, traditional FoMs do not accurately describe the trade-off between key instrumental parameters. As such, we present the development of a FoM which can directly relate antenna pattern characteristics to their effect on CMB observations.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Space Launch Infrastructure – A Techno-Economic Analysis
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Space access infrastructure can now outperform rockets on levelized cost per kilogram. The architecture with the lowest technology adaptation degree of difficulty in the field of electromagnetics is shown to be the Tethered Ring. A Tethered Ring is a dynamic structure that can be built on Earth and raised into the stratosphere without a pre-existing space infrastructure, a space-based industry, or any need for expensive rocket launch services. It can support facilities (for example, launch systems, transit systems, communications gear, and habitable spaces) at an altitude of 32km and at an estimated capital cost of under ${\$}110$ per kg supported.

articleTitle: Spherical Near Field to Far Field Transformation Algorithm for Offset-Mounted Antennas on Metallic Ground
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: With regard to the spherical near-field measurement of on-board and airborne antennas, the floor of the test site is mostly replaced by metallic plane, which not only facilitates the movement of large carriers but also narrows the test space. However, it will lead to difficulty in recovering the spherical mode coefficients (SMC) of the antenna under test (AUT) from the superimposed near field on the upper hemisphere, extrapolating the far field in free zone. Furthermore, due to physical constraints, the AUT will generally deviate from the scan center, inducing an increment of the required samples for solving SMC. Therefore, a transformation algorithm is proposed in this paper, which can be applied to the near field on the measurement sphere of the offset antenna above the PEC plane to acquire the three-dimensional radiation characteristics in free space at a lower oversampling rate. The boundary conditions of the electric field of the PEC plane are fulfilled by imposing the image principle on the spherical modes. With the introduction of rotation and translation operators, the relationship of SMC in the global and eccentric coordinate system is investigated, enabling the algorithm to effectively minimize the quantity of unknown SMC. Moreover, when combined with the igloo sampling grid, the oversampling rate for retrieving SMC can be further decreased, thus shortening the measurement time. While the test site contains metallic ground, the numerical results demonstrate the capability of the presented method to derive the SMC of the offset antenna and extrapolate the far field in free space.

articleTitle: An Application of the L4± Numbers in the Theory of Azimuthally Magnetized Ferrite-Dielectric Circular Waveguides
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The real positive $\bar{L}_{4\pm}=\bar{L}_{4\pm}(c,\overline{\bar{\varepsilon}},\rho,\alpha_{\pm},n)$ numbers ($c=3,\overline{\bar{\varepsilon}},\quad \rho,\quad \alpha_{\pm}-$real, $\overline{\bar{\varepsilon}}\gt1,\quad 0\lt\rho\lt1,\ -1\lt\alpha_{-}\lt0,0\lt\alpha_{+}\lt1,\alpha_{\pm}\neq 0,n=1,2,3\ldots$, are advanced as limits in case $ k_{+}\rightarrow+\infty$ and $k_{-}\rightarrow-\infty\quad (k_{+}\gt0,k_{-}\lt0$) of the products of the infinitely large quantities $|k_{\pm}|,|a_{\pm}|$or $|a_{\pm}-1|$ by the positive purely imaginary zeros $\overline{\bar{\eta}}_{k_{\pm},n}^{(c)}(\overline{\bar{\varepsilon}},\rho,\alpha_{\pm})$ (infinitesimal on the same condition for $k_{\pm}$) in the variable x (z) of a transcendental function $\overline{\bar{F}}_{4}(a,c;x,\overline{\bar{\varepsilon}},\rho,\alpha)$, formed through complex Kummer and Tricomi confluent hypergeometric $\Phi(a,c;x)$ and $\Psi(a,c;x)$, and real ordinary Bessel $J_{m}(y)$ functions $(a=c/2-jk,x=jz,k,y,z$ - real, $-\infty\lt k\lt+\infty,\quad y\gt0,\quad z\gt0,\quad y=\rho\overline{\bar{q}}z,\overline{\overline{\bar{q}}}=\overline{\bar{q}}(\overline{\bar{\varepsilon}},\alpha,k),\overline{\bar{q}}\gt0,\ m=0,1)$. The values of $\bar{L}_{4\pm}$ are found, using a special iterative technique. The effect of parameters $\overline{\bar{\varepsilon}}$ and $\rho$ on them is studied for fixed $|\alpha_{\pm}|$, assuming $n=1$. The identity $\overline{\bar{F}}_{4}(a,c;x,\overline{\bar{\varepsilon}},\rho,\alpha)=0$ is interpreted as characteristic equation of the circular waveguide, comprising a coaxial dielectric cylinder and a ferrite toroid with azimuthal bias that sustains normal $TE_{0\text{n}}$ modes, and $\overline{\bar{\eta}}_{k_{\pm},n}^{(c)}(\overline{\bar{\varepsilon}},\rho,\alpha_{\pm})$(the roots of equation) as portrait of its eigenvalue spectrum. The $\overline{\bar{L}}_{4\pm}$ numbers are regarded as mathematical image of the upper cut-off frequencies of configuration, $\overline{\bar{\eta}}_{0,n}^{(c)}(\overline{\bar{\varepsilon}},\rho,\alpha_{\pm})$- of its lower ones $(\overline{\bar{\varepsilon}}-$ dielectric $\varepsilon_{d}$ to ferrite $\varepsilon_{r}$ relative permittivity ratio, $\rho$ - factor of filling with dielectric, $\alpha_{\pm}-$off-diagonal ferrite permeability tensor element, n-order of the mode, $k,y,z-$ functions of the phase constant, structure parameters and frequency). The subscripts “±” show the direction of magnetization of anisotropic load $(\operatorname{sgn}k=\operatorname{sgn}\alpha)$. The condition $\overline{\bar{\varepsilon}}\gt1(\varepsilon_{d}\gt\varepsilon_{r})$ is essential. In general, $\overline{\bar{L}}_{4+}\neq\overline{\bar{L}}_{4-}$ and $\overline{\bar{L}}_{4\pm}\gt\overline{\bar{\eta}}_{0,n}^{(c)}$. For each $|\alpha_{\pm}|$there are two upper and one lower cut-off frequency that differ, except the first in some isolated cases. The criterion for phase shifter operation of the geometry is derived. The upper and lower cut-off frequencies and the width of the area where it exhibits phase shifting properties are reckoned in normalized form for the TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</inf> mode, depending on $\overline{\bar{\varepsilon}},\phi_{\pm}\mid$and $\rho$.

articleTitle: Some Features of the Circular Ferrite-Dielectric Waveguide Phase Shifter of Azimuthal Magnetization
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The lower and upper cut-off frequencies and the width of the work area of a digital phase shifter, built on a circular waveguide, containing a co-axially positioned azimuthally magnetized latching ferrite cylinder and a dielectric toroid, under normal TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</inf> mode excitation, are investigated. The size of anisotropic region is assumed large and the relative permittivities of both strata–equal. The off-diagonal element of ferrite permeability tensor changes in the whole interval in which it has sense. The analysis is based on the characteristic equation of the structure, derived earlier in terms of complex Kummer confluent hypergeometric and real ordinary Bessel and Neumann functions, and on its phase curves, plotted before, too. It indicates that for any set of parameters the transmission line has one lower and two upper cut-off frequencies. They specify the condition for phase shifter operation of the device and the width of the area in that it is fulfilled. The lower frequencies are determined with the help of the roots $\bar{\xi}_{0, n}^{(c)}$ of the equation mentioned in its purely imaginary independent variable, computed for a zero value of the imaginary part of the complex first parameter of Kummer functions. The upperby means of the real positive $\overline{L}_{3\pm}$ numbers, advanced recently by the authors, calculated, using the same roots, but for infinitely large positive and negative numerical equivalents of the imaginary part referred to. Detailed computations of $\bar{\xi}_{0, n}^{(c)}$ and $\overline{L}_{3\pm}$, of the cut-off frequencies and of the width of the area in question are performed. The effect of off-diagonal tensor element on all results is studied. It is established that in certain cases the configuration does not provide phase shift at all.

articleTitle: GNSS-based End-of-Train Device Performance Evaluation and Improvement by Means of Particle Filter Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The Train Integrity Monitoring System (TIMS) function is becoming more and more demanding for the next generation for train control (NGTC) in both China and European train control systems. Traditional train integrity detection provides the integrity status of the train by monitoring the status of brake pipe pressure without adding equipment a major the train, but not possible to provide redundancy to meet the SIL 4 (Safety Integrity Level 4) requirement of the train control system<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[1]</sup>. GNSS-based train localization provides essential location and velocity data for each wagon, the information transmitted to head-of-train (HOT) device, then the integrity can be determined. End-of-Train (EOT) device is normally mounted on the coupler of the last wagon, the observation condition for GNSS is not good, normally “half-sky”. In view of the above conditions, this paper constructs three different constraint scenarios: open sky, general constraint and severe constraint based on the laboratory GNSS simulator by setting the EOT user antenna directivity pattern, and evaluates the positioning accuracy in the constraint scenarios. On this basis, the state equation and observation equation of the system are established with a simulation example, and the positioning results are optimized by using the particle filter algorithm. The results show that the average location error in the unobstructed scenario is 0.12m; The average value of general constraint error is 3.93m, and the average value of error after pf processing is 3.02m; The mean value of severe constraint location error is 11.94m, and 8.83m after PF filtering. This filtering algorithm can improve the location accuracy to a certain extent.
